metadata.title: Square function estimates for discrete Radon transforms

nodes.name: Calderon-Zygmund kernel conditions
nodes.statement_short: $K$ is a $\calC^1$ Calderon-Zygmund kernel obeying the standard size/gradient bound and a uniform truncated-integral cancellation bound.

nodes.name: Polynomial mapping $\calP$
nodes.statement: Let $\calP=(\calP_1,\ldots, \calP_{d_0}): \ZZ^{k} \rightarrow \ZZ^{d_0}$ be a mapping where each component $\calP_j:\ZZ^{k} \rightarrow \ZZ$ is an integer-valued polynomial of $k$ variables with $\calP_j(0) = 0$.
differentia: each component $\calP_j:\ZZ^{k} \rightarrow \ZZ$ is an integer-valued polynomial of $k$ variables

nodes.name: Discrete singular Radon transform $T^{\calP}$
nodes.statement: In the present article, as in \cite{iw}, we are interested in the discrete singular Radon transform $T^{\calP}$ defined by \begin{align} T^{\calP} f(x) = \sum_{y\in\ZZ^k\setminus\{0\}} f\big(x - \calP(y)\big) K(y) \end{align} for a finitely supported function $f: \ZZ^{d_0} \rightarrow \RR$.
nodes.statement_short: Convolution-type discrete singular integral along the polynomial orbit $\calP(y)$, $y\in\ZZ^k\setminus\{0\}$.

nodes.name: Theorem A ($\ell^p$ boundedness of $T^{\calP}$)
nodes.statement: For every $p \in (1, \infty)$ there is $C_p > 0$ such that for all $f \in \ell^p\big(\ZZ^{d_0}\big)$ \begin{align} \big\lVert T^\calP f \big\rVert_{\ell^p} \leq C_p \vnorm{f}_{\ell^p}. \end{align} Moreover, the constant $C_p$ is independent of the coefficients of the polynomial mapping $\calP$.
nodes.statement_short: $T^{\calP}$ is bounded on $\ell^p(\ZZ^{d_0})$ for every $p\in(1,\infty)$, uniformly in the coefficients of $\calP$.
conclusions: the constant $C_p$ is independent of the coefficients of the polynomial mapping $\calP$

nodes.name: Attribution of Theorem A to Ionescu and Wainger
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{thm:0} was proven by Ionescu and Wainger in \cite{iw}.

nodes.name: Continuous Radon transform $R^{\calP}$
nodes.statement: The operator $T^{\calP}$ is a discrete analogue of the continuous Radon transform $R^{\calP}$ defined by \begin{align} R^{\calP}f(x) ={\rm p.v.}\int_{\RR^k} f\big(x - \calP(y)\big) K(y){\rm d}y. \end{align}
nodes.origin_citation: Stein, Harmonic Analysis; Christ, Nagel, Stein & Wainger

nodes.name: Dyadic decomposition of a Calderon-Zygmund kernel
nodes.statement_short: Any CZ kernel splits as $K=\sum_n K_n$ with $K_n$ supported on the dyadic annulus $2^{n-2}\le|x|\le 2^n$, uniformly CZ-bounded, and (for $n\ge1$) of mean zero.
nodes.section: Outline of the strategy of our proof
nodes.origin_citation: Stein, Harmonic Analysis (Big Stein), Ch. 6 §4.5 and Ch. 13 §5.3

nodes.name: Dyadic pieces $T_n^{\calP}$
nodes.statement: \begin{align} T_n^{\calP} f(x) = \sum_{y\in\ZZ^k} f\big(x - \calQ(y)\big) K_n(y) \end{align} for each $n\in\ZZ$.
nodes.section: Outline of the strategy of our proof

nodes.name: Reduction of Theorem A to the dyadic-piece estimate
nodes.statement: Thus in view of \eqref{eq:88}, instead of \eqref{eq:35}, it suffices to show that for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that \begin{align} \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}T_n^{\calP}f\Big\|_{\ell^p}\le C_p\|f\|_{\ell^p} \end{align} for all $f\in\ell^p\big(\ZZ^d\big)$,
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to bound $\sum_{n\ge0}T_n^{\calP}$ on $\ell^p$ instead of $T^{\calP}$.
nodes.section: Outline of the strategy of our proof

nodes.name: Projections $\Xi_n$ (outline form)
nodes.statement: Namely, let $\eta$ be a smooth bump function with a small support, fix $l \in \NN$ and define for each integer $n\ge0$ the following projections \begin{align} \Xi_{n}(\xi) =\sum_{a/q \in\mathscr{U}_{n^l}} \eta\big(\mathcal E_n^{-1}(\xi - a/q)\big) \end{align} where $\mathcal E_n$ is a diagonal $d\times d$ matrix with positive entries $\big(\varepsilon_{j}: 1\le j\le d\big)$ such that $\varepsilon_{j}\le e^{-n^{1/5}}$ and \[ \mathscr{U}_{n^l}=\big\{a/q \in \TT^d\cap\QQ^d : a=(a_1, \ldots, a_d) \in \NN^d_q \text{ and } \mathrm{gcd}(a_1, \ldots, a_d, q)=1 \text{ and } q\in P_{n^l}\big\} \] for some family $P_{n^l}$ such that $\NN_{n^l}\subseteq P_{n^l}\subseteq \NN_{e^{n^{1/10}}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Major-arc projections localising the multiplier $m_n$ near rationals $a/q$ with $q$ in a fattened family $P_{n^l}$.
nodes.section: Outline of the strategy of our proof

nodes.name: Logarithmic $\ell^p$ bound for the projections $\Xi_n$
nodes.statement: Exploiting the ideas of Ionescu and Wainger from \cite{iw}, we prove that for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $C_{l, p}>0$ such that \begin{align} \big\|\calF^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\le C_{l, p}\log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The projection $\Xi_n$ is $\ell^p$-bounded with only a $\log(n+2)$ loss.
nodes.section: Outline of the strategy of our proof

nodes.name: Multipliers $\Delta_{n, s}^j$ (outline form)
nodes.statement: For this purpose we construct new multipliers of the form \begin{align} \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(\mathcal E_{n+j}(\xi-a/q)\big)-\eta\big(\mathcal E_{n+j+1}(\xi-a/q)\big)\big)\eta\big(\mathcal E_{s}(\xi-a/q)\big) \end{align} such that \[ \Xi_n(\xi)\simeq\sum_{j\in\ZZ}\sum_{s\ge0}\Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi). \]
nodes.statement_short: Littlewood-Paley-type pieces of $\Xi_n$ indexed by scale $j$ and denominator level $s$.
nodes.section: Outline of the strategy of our proof

nodes.name: Robust $\ell^2$ square function estimate for $m_n\Delta_{n,s}^j$
nodes.statement: This is the key ingredient in our proof which combined with the robust $\ell^2\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ estimate \begin{align} \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\ZZ}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^j\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^2} \le C2^{-\varepsilon|j|}(s+1)^{-\delta l} \|f\|_{\ell^2} \end{align} allows us to deduce \eqref{eq:32}.
nodes.statement_short: The $\ell^2$ square function built from $m_n\Delta_{n,s}^j$ decays geometrically in $|j|$ and polynomially in $s$.
nodes.section: Outline of the strategy of our proof

nodes.name: Averaging Radon operators $M_N^{\calP}$
nodes.statement: the averaging Radon operators \begin{align} M_N^{\calP} f(x) =N^{-k} \sum_{y\in\NN_N^k} f\big(x-\calP(y)\big) \end{align} where $\NN^k_N = \{1, 2, \ldots, N\}^k$,
nodes.section: Outline of the strategy of our proof

nodes.name: Truncated singular Radon transforms $T_N^{\calP}$
nodes.statement: and the truncated singular Radon transforms \begin{align} T_N^{\calP} f(x) = \sum_{y\in\mathbb B_N\setminus\{0\}} f\big(x - \calP(y)\big) K(y) \end{align} where $\mathbb B_N=\{x\in\ZZ^k: |x|\le N\}$.
nodes.section: Outline of the strategy of our proof

nodes.name: Multi-index set $\Gamma$ and dimension $d$
nodes.statement: We set \[ N_0 = \max\{ \deg \calP_j : 1 \leq j \leq d_0\} \] and define the set \[ \Gamma = \big\{ \gamma \in \ZZ^k \setminus\{0\} : 0 \leq \gamma_j \leq N_0 \text{ for each } j = 1, \ldots, k \big\} \] with the lexicographic order. Let $d$ be the cardinality of $\Gamma$.

nodes.name: Canonical polynomial mapping $\calQ$ and anisotropic dilations $t^A$
nodes.statement: Next we introduce the canonical polynomial mapping $$ \calQ = \big(\seq{\calQ_\gamma}{\gamma \in \Gamma}\big) : \ZZ^k \rightarrow \ZZ^d $$ where $\calQ_\gamma(x) = x^\gamma$ and $x^\gamma=x_1^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot x_k^{\gamma_k}$. The canonical polynomial mapping $\calQ$ determines anisotropic dilations. Namely, let $A$ be a diagonal $d \times d$ matrix such that $$ (A v)_\gamma = \abs{\gamma} v_\gamma $$ for any $v\in\RR^d$ and $\gamma\in\Gamma$, where $|\gamma|=\gamma_1+\ldots+\gamma_k$. Then for every $t > 0$ we set $$ t^{A}=\exp(A\log t) $$ i.e. $t^A x=(t^{|\gamma|}x_{\gamma}: \gamma\in \Gamma)$ for $x\in\RR^d$ and we see that $\calQ(tx)=t^A\calQ(x)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\calQ$ collects all monomials $x^\gamma$, $\gamma\in\Gamma$, and is homogeneous for the anisotropic dilations $t^A$.

nodes.name: Linear transformation $L$ with $L\calQ = \calP$
nodes.statement: Observe also that each $\calP_j$ can be expressed as $$ \calP_j(x) = \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} c_j^\gamma x^\gamma $$ for some $c_j^\gamma \in \RR$. Moreover, the coefficients $\big(\seq{c_j^\gamma}{\gamma \in \Gamma, j \in \{1, \ldots, d_0\}}\big)$ define a linear transformation $L: \RR^d \rightarrow \RR^{d_0}$ such that $L\calQ = \calP$. Indeed, it is enough to set $$ (L v)_j = \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} c_j^\gamma v_\gamma $$ for each $j \in \{1, \ldots, d_0\}$ and $v \in \RR^d$.
nodes.statement_short: Every polynomial mapping $\calP$ factors as a linear image $L\calQ$ of the canonical mapping.
assumptions: each $\calP_j$ can be expressed as $\calP_j(x) = \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} c_j^\gamma x^\gamma$ for some $c_j^\gamma \in \RR$
conclusions: the coefficients $\big(\seq{c_j^\gamma}{\gamma \in \Gamma, j \in \{1, \ldots, d_0\}}\big)$ define a linear transformation $L: \RR^d \rightarrow \RR^{d_0}$ such that $L\calQ = \calP$

nodes.name: Theorem B ($\ell^p$ boundedness of $T^{\calQ}$)
nodes.statement: For every $p \in (1, \infty)$ there is $C_p > 0$ such that for all $f \in \ell^p\big(\ZZ^{d}\big)$ \begin{align} \big\lVert T^\calQ f \big\rVert_{\ell^p} \leq C_p \vnorm{f}_{\ell^p}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The discrete singular Radon transform along the canonical mapping $\calQ$ is $\ell^p(\ZZ^d)$ bounded.

nodes.name: Lifting procedure reducing $\calP$ to $\calQ$
nodes.statement: In view of \cite[Section 11]{bigs} we can perform some lifting procedure which allows us to replace the underlying polynomial mapping $\calP$ from \eqref{eq:35} by the canonical polynomial mapping $\calQ$. Moreover, it shows that \eqref{eq:37} implies \eqref{eq:35} with the same constant $C_p$, see also \cite{iw} for more details. Therefore, the matters are reduced to proving \eqref{eq:37} for the canonical polynomial mapping. The advantage of working with the canonical polynomial mapping $\calQ$ is that it has all coefficients equal to $1$, and the uniform bound in this case is immediate. From now on for simplicity of notation we will write $T=T^{\calQ}$.
nodes.statement_short: A lifting argument shows Theorem B implies Theorem A with the same constant.
nodes.origin_citation: Stein, Harmonic Analysis, Section 11; Ionescu & Wainger

nodes.name: Notation: $\NN_N$ and the norms on $\RR^d$
nodes.statement:
Let $\NN_0 = \NN \cup \{0\}$ and for $N \in \NN$ we set \[ \NN_N =  ig\{1, 2, \ldots, N ig\}. \] For a vector $x \in \RR^d$ we will use the following norms \[ 
orm{x}_\infty = \max\{\abs{x_j} : 1 \leq j \leq d\}, \quad 	ext{and} \quad 
orm{x} = \Big(\sum_{j = 1}^d \abs{x_j}^2\Big)^{1/2}. \] If $\gamma$ is a multi-index from $\NN_0^k$ then $
orm{\gamma} = \gamma_1 + \ldots + \gamma_k$.

nodes.name: Fourier transform $\calF$ and Fourier coefficients $\hat f$
nodes.statement: For a function $f \in L^1\big(\RR^d\big)$ let $\calF$ denote the Fourier transform on $\RR^d$ defined as $$ \calF f(\xi) = \int_{\RR^d} f(x) e^{2\pi i \sprod{\xi}{x}} {\rm d}x. $$ If $f \in \ell^1\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ we set $$ \hat{f}(\xi) = \sum_{x \in \ZZ^d} f(x) e^{2\pi i \sprod{\xi}{x}}. $$ To simplify the notation we denote by $\mathcal F^{-1}$ the inverse Fourier transform on $\RR^d$ and the inverse Fourier transform on the torus $\TT^d\equiv[0, 1)^d$ (Fourier coefficients). The meaning of $\calF^{-1}$ will be always clear from the context.

nodes.name: Smooth bump function $\eta$
nodes.statement: Let $\eta: \RR^d \rightarrow \RR$ be a smooth function such that $0 \leq \eta(x) \leq 1$ and \[ \eta(x) = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{ for } \norm{x} \leq 1/(16 d),\\ 0 & \text{ for } \norm{x} \geq 1/(8 d). \end{cases} \]

nodes.name: Remark 2.1 (factorization $\eta=\phi*\psi$)
nodes.statement: We will additionally assume that $\eta$ is a convolution of two non-negative smooth functions $\phi$ and $\psi$ with compact supports contained in $(-1/(8d), 1/(8d))^d$.

nodes.name: Parameters $\rho$, $N_0$, $Q_0$, $D$ and the prime set $\mathbb P_N$
nodes.statement: Let $\rho>0$ and for every $N\in\NN$ define \[ N_0=\lfloor N^{\rho/2}\rfloor+1 \qquad \text{and} \qquad Q_0=(N_0!)^D \] where $D=D_{\rho}=\lfloor 2/\rho\rfloor+1$. Let $\mathbb P_N=\mathbb P\cap (N_0, N]$ where $\mathbb P$ is the set of all prime numbers.

nodes.name: The set $\Pi(V)$ of bounded-length prime products
nodes.statement: For any $V\subseteq\mathbb P_N$ we define \[ \Pi(V)=\bigcup_{k\in\NN_D}\Pi_k(V) \] where for any $k\in\NN_D$ \[ \Pi_k(V)=\big\{p_{1}^{\gamma_{1}}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_{k}}: \ \gamma_{l}\in\NN_D\ \text{and}\ p_{l}\in V\ \text{are distinct for all $1\le l\le k$} \big\}. \] In other words $\Pi(V)$ is the set of all products of primes factors from $V$ of length at most $D$, at powers between $1$ and $D$.
nodes.genus: the set of all products of primes factors from $V$
differentia: of length at most $D$, at powers between $1$ and $D$

nodes.name: The denominator set $P_N$
nodes.statement: Now we introduce the sets \[ P_N=\big\{q=Q\cdot w: Q|Q_0\ \text{and}\ w\in \Pi(\mathbb P_{N})\cup\{1\}\big\}. \]

nodes.name: Unique factorization $q=Q\cdot w$ and the inclusions $\NN_N\subseteq P_N\subseteq\NN_{e^{N^{\rho}}}$
nodes.statement: It is not difficult to see that every integer $q\in\NN_N$ can be uniquely written as $q=Q\cdot w$ where $Q|Q_0$ and $w\in \Pi(\mathbb P_N)\cup\{1\}$. Moreover, for sufficiently large $N\in\NN$ we have \[q=Q\cdot w\le Q_0\cdot w\le (N_0!)^DN^{D^2}\le e^{N^{\rho}} \] thus we have $\NN_N\subseteq P_N\subseteq\NN_{e^{N^{\rho}}}$. Furthermore, if $N_1\le N_2$ then $P_{N_1}\subseteq P_{N_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: $P_N$ contains $\NN_N$, is contained in $\NN_{e^{N^\rho}}$, and is increasing in $N$.
conclusions: $q\in\NN_N$ can be uniquely written as $q=Q\cdot w$ where $Q|Q_0$ and $w\in \Pi(\mathbb P_N)\cup\{1\}$

nodes.name: Rational sets $\mathcal R(S)$, $A_q$ and $\mathscr{U}_N$
nodes.statement: For a subset $S\subseteq\NN$ we define \[ \mathcal R(S)=\big\{a/q \in \TT^d\cap\QQ^d : a \in A_q \text{ and } q\in S\big\} \] where for each $q\in\NN$ \[ A_q=\big\{a\in\NN_q^d: \mathrm{gcd}\big(q, \mathrm(a_{\gamma}: \gamma\in\Gamma)\big)\big\}. \] Finally, for each $N\in\NN$ we will consider the sets \begin{align} \mathscr{U}_N=\mathcal R(P_N). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $\mathscr U_N$ is the set of reduced rationals in $\TT^d$ whose denominator lies in $P_N$.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $\mathscr{U}_N$
nodes.statement: It is easy to see, if $N_1\le N_2$ then $\mathscr{U}_{N_1}\subseteq \mathscr{U}_{N_2}$.

nodes.name: $L^p$-bounded multiplier $\Theta$ with constant $\boldA_p$
nodes.statement: We will assume that $\Theta$ is a multiplier on $\RR^d$ and for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $\boldA_p >0 $ such that for every $f\in L^2\big(\RR^d\big)\cap L^p\big(\RR^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \big\lVert\calF^{-1}\big(\Theta\mathcal F f\big)\big\rVert_{L^p} \leq \boldA_p \vnorm{f}_{L^p}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $\Theta$ is a continuous $L^p(\RR^d)$ multiplier with norm $\boldA_p$.

nodes.name: Periodic multipliers $\Delta_N$
nodes.statement: For each $N \in \NN$ we define new periodic multipliers \begin{align} \Delta_N(\xi) =\sum_{a/q \in\mathscr{U}_N} \Theta(\xi - a/q) \eta_N(\xi - a/q) \end{align} where $\eta_N(\xi)=\eta\big(\mathcal E_N^{-1}\xi\big)$ and $\mathcal E_N$ is a diagonal $d\times d$ matrix with positive entries $(\varepsilon_{\gamma}: \gamma\in\Gamma)$ such that $\varepsilon_{\gamma} \le e^{-N^{2\rho}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Periodization of $\Theta$ against narrow bumps centred at all rationals in $\mathscr U_N$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (Ionescu-Wainger type multiplier theorem)
nodes.statement: Let $\Theta$ be a multiplier on $\RR^d$ obeying \eqref{eq:155}. Then for every $\rho>0$ and $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $C_{\rho, p} > 0$ such that for any $N\in\NN$ and $f \in \ell^p\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ \begin{align} \big\lVert \calF^{-1}\big(\Delta_{N} \hat{f}\big)\big\rVert_{\ell^p} \leq C_{\rho, p} (\boldA_p+1)\log N \vnorm{f}_{\ell^p}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The discrete periodized multiplier $\Delta_N$ is $\ell^p(\ZZ^d)$-bounded with only a $\log N$ loss over the continuous norm $\boldA_p$.

nodes.name: Proof strategy for Theorem 1
nodes.statement: The main constructing blocks have been gathered in the next three subsections. Theorem \ref{th:3} is a consequence of Theorem \ref{thm:5} and Proposition \ref{prop:5} proved below. To prove Theorem \ref{th:3} we find some $C_{\rho}>0$ and disjoint sets $\mathscr{U}_N^i\subseteq\mathscr{U}_N$ such that \[ \mathscr{U}_N=\bigcup_{1\le i\le C_{\rho}\log N}\mathscr{U}_N^i \] and we show that $\Delta_N$ with the summation restricted to $\mathscr{U}_N^i$ is bounded on $\ell^p\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ for every $p\in(1, \infty)$. In order to construct $\mathscr{U}_N^i$ we need a suitable partition of integers from the set $\Pi(\mathbb P_{N})\cup\{1\}$, see also \cite{iw}.
nodes.statement_short: Partition $\mathscr U_N$ into $C_\rho\log N$ disjoint pieces and bound each restricted multiplier uniformly.

nodes.name: Definition 2.1 ($\mathcal O$ property)
nodes.statement: A subset $\Lambda\subseteq \Pi(V)$ has $\mathcal O$ property if there is $k\in\NN_D$ and there are sets $S_1, S_2,\ldots, S_k$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] for each $1\le j\le k$ there is $ \beta_j\in\NN$ such that $S_j=\{q_{j, 1},\ldots, q_{j, \beta_j}\}$; \item[(ii)] for every $q_{j, s}\in S_j$ there are $p_{j, s}\in V$ and $\gamma_j\in\NN_D$ such that $q_{j, s}=p_{j, s}^{\gamma_j}$; \item[(iii)] for every $w\in W$ there are unique numbers $q_{1, s_1}\in S_1,\ldots, q_{k, s_k}\in S_k$ such that $w=q_{1, s_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot q_{k, s_k}$; \item[(iv)] if $(j, s)\not=(j', s')$ then $(q_{j, s}, q_{j', s'})=1$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: $\Lambda$ has $\mathcal O$ property when its elements factor uniquely as products of pairwise coprime prime powers drawn one from each of $k$ fixed families $S_1,\ldots,S_k$.
differentia: for each $1\le j\le k$ there is $ \beta_j\in\NN$ such that $S_j=\{q_{j, 1},\ldots, q_{j, \beta_j}\}$
for every $q_{j, s}\in S_j$ there are $p_{j, s}\in V$ and $\gamma_j\in\NN_D$ such that $q_{j, s}=p_{j, s}^{\gamma_j}$
for every $w\in W$ there are unique numbers $q_{1, s_1}\in S_1,\ldots, q_{k, s_k}\in S_k$ such that $w=q_{1, s_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot q_{k, s_k}$

nodes.name: Three comments on the $\mathcal O$ property
nodes.statement: Now three comments are in order. \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] The set $\Lambda=\{1\}$ has $\mathcal O$ property corresponding to $k=0$. \item[(ii)] If $\Lambda$ has $\mathcal O$ property, then each subset $\Lambda'\subseteq \Lambda$ has $\mathcal O$ property as well. \item[(iii)] If a set $\Lambda$ has $\mathcal O$ property then each element of $\Lambda$ has the same number of prime factors $k\le D$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: The $\mathcal O$ property is hereditary under subsets, holds trivially for $\{1\}$, and forces a common number of prime factors.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.1 (fundamental combinatorial lemma)
nodes.statement: For every $\rho>0$ there exists a constant $C_{\rho}>0$ such that for every $N\in\NN$ the set $\mathscr{U}_N$ can be written as a disjoint union of at most $C_{\rho}\log N$ sets $\mathscr{U}_N^i=\mathcal R(P_N^i)$ where \begin{align} P_N^i =\big\{ q=Q\cdot w: Q|Q_0\ \text{and}\ w\in {\Lambda}_i(\mathbb P_N)\big\} \end{align} and ${\Lambda}_i(\mathbb P_N) \subseteq \Pi(\mathbb P_N)\cup\{1\}$ has $\mathcal O$ property for each integer $1\le i\le C_{\rho}\log N$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathscr U_N$ splits into at most $C_\rho\log N$ disjoint pieces, each generated by a set with the $\mathcal O$ property.
conclusions: the set $\mathscr{U}_N$ can be written as a disjoint union of at most $C_{\rho}\log N$ sets $\mathscr{U}_N^i=\mathcal R(P_N^i)$
${\Lambda}_i(\mathbb P_N) \subseteq \Pi(\mathbb P_N)\cup\{1\}$ has $\mathcal O$ property for each integer $1\le i\le C_{\rho}\log N$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement:
We have to prove that for every $V\subseteq \mathbb P_N$ the set $\Pi(V)$ can be written as a disjoint union of at most $C_k\log N$ sets with $\mathcal O$ property. Fix $k\in\NN_D$, let $\gamma=(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k)\in\NN_D^k$ be a multi-index and observe that \[ \Pi_k(V)= igcup_{\gamma\in\NN_D^k}\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V) \] where \[ \Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)= ig\{p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}:\ 	ext{$p_l\in V$ are distinct for all $1\le l\le k$}  ig\}. \] Since there are $D^k$ possible choices of exponents $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k\in\NN_D$ when $k\in\NN_D$, it only suffices to prove that every $\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$ can be partitioned into a union (not necessarily disjoint) of at most $C_k\log N$ sets with $\mathcal O$ property. We claim that for each $k\in\NN$ there is a constant $C_k>0$ and a family  egin{align} \pi= ig\{\pi_i(V): 1\le i\le C_k\log |V| ig\} \end{align} of partitions of $V$ such that  egin{itemize} \item[(i)] for every $1\le i\le C_k\log |V|$ each $\pi_i(V)=\{V_1^i,\ldots, V_k^i\}$ consists of pairwise disjoint subsets of $V$ and $V=V_1^i\cup\ldots\cup V_k^i$; \item[(ii)] for every $E\subseteq V$ with at least $k$ elements there exists $\pi_i(V)=\{V_1^i,\ldots, V_k^i\}\in\pi$ such that $E\cap V_j^i
ot=\emptyset$ for every $1\le j\le k$. \end{itemize} Assume for a moment we have constructed a family $\pi$ as in \eqref{eq:11}. Then one sees that for a fixed $\gamma\in\NN_D^k$ we have  egin{align} \Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)= igcup_{1\le i\le C_{k}\log |V|}\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V) \end{align} where \[ \Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)= ig\{p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}: p_{j}^{\gamma_j}\in  ig(V\cap V_j^i)^{\gamma_j} 	ext{ and $V_j^i\in\pi_i(V)$ for each $1\le j\le k$} ig\} \] and $ ig(V\cap V_j^i)^{\gamma_j}=\{p^{\gamma_j}: p\in V\cap V_j^i\} $. Indeed, the sum on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:28} is contained in $\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$ since each $\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)$ is. For the opposite inclusion take $p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}\in\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$ and let $E=\{p_1,\ldots, p_k\}$, then property (ii) for the family \eqref{eq:11} ensures that there is $\pi_i(V)=\{V_1^i,\ldots, V_k^i\}\in\pi$ such that $E\cap V_j^i
ot=\emptyset$ for every $1\le j\le k$. Therefore, $p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}\in\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)$. Furthermore, we see that for each $1\le i\le C_k\log N$ the sets $\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)$ have $\mathcal O$ property. The proof will be completed if we construct the family $\pi$ as in \eqref{eq:11} for the set $V$. We assume, for simplicity, that $V=\NN_N$ but the result is true for all $V\subseteq \NN_N$ containing at least $k$ elements. Now it will be more comfortable to work with surjective mappings $f:\NN_N\mapsto\NN_k$ rather than with partitions of $\NN_N$ into $k$ non-empty subsets. It will cause no changes to us, since every surjection $f:\NN_N\mapsto\NN_k$ determines a partition $\{f^{-1}[\{m\}]: 1\le m\le k\}$ of $\NN_N$ into $k$ non-empty subsets. For the proof we employ a probabilistic argument. Indeed, let $f:\NN_N\mapsto \NN_k$ be a random surjective mapping. Assume that for every $n\in\NN_N$ and $m\in\NN_k$ we have $\mathds{P}(\{f(n)=m\})=1/k$ independently of all other $n\in\NN_N$. For every $E\subseteq\NN_N$ with $k$ elements we have $\mathds P(\{|f[E]|=k\})=k!/k^k$. It suffices to show that for some $r\simeq_k\log N$ and $f_1, \ldots, f_r$ random surjections we have \[ \mathds P(\{ orall_{E\subseteq\NN_N}\ |E|=k\ \exists _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|=k\})>0. \] In other words, for each $E\subseteq\NN_N$ with cardinality $k$ it is always possible to find, with a positive probability, among at most $C_k\log N$ random surjections at least one $f:\NN_N\mapsto \NN_k$ such that $|f[E]|=k$. Then the set $\{f^{-1}[\{m\}]: 1\le m\le k\}$ is a partition of $\NN_N$ and $E\cap f^{-1}[\{m\}]
ot=\emptyset$ for every $1\le m\le k$. The task now is the determine the exact value of $r\simeq_k\log N$. Take now $1\le r\le N$ independent random surjections $f_1, \ldots, f_r$ and observe that  egin{multline*} \mathds P(\{\exists_{E\subseteq\NN_N}\ |E|=k\  orall _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|<k\})\le \sum_{E\subseteq \NN_N:\: |E|=k} \mathds P(\{ orall _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|<k\}) \ =\sum_{E\subseteq \NN_N:\: |E|=k} igg(1- rac{k!}{k^k} igg)^r= inom{N}{k} igg(1- rac{k!}{k^k} igg)^r \le igg( rac{eN}{k} igg)^ke^{-r rac{k!}{k^k}} =e^{k\log( rac{eN}{k})-r rac{k!}{k^k}}. \end{multline*} Therefore \[ \mathds P(\{\exists_{E\subseteq\NN_N}\ |E|=k\  orall _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|<k\})<1 \] if and only if \[ r> rac{k^{k+1}}{k!}\log igg( rac{eN}{k} igg). \] Thus taking \[ r= igg\lceil rac{k^{k+1}}{k!}\log igg( rac{eN}{k} igg) iggceil+1\simeq C_k\log N \] we see that it does the job. This completes the proof of Lemma ef{lem:12}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to partitioning each $\Pi_k^\gamma(V)$, then produce $C_k\log N$ random surjections $\NN_N\to\NN_k$ that jointly separate every $k$-element set, by a first-moment (union bound) argument.

nodes.name: Reduce to partitioning $\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$
nodes.statement: We have to prove that for every $V\subseteq \mathbb P_N$ the set $\Pi(V)$ can be written as a disjoint union of at most $C_k\log N$ sets with $\mathcal O$ property. Fix $k\in\NN_D$, let $\gamma=(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k)\in\NN_D^k$ be a multi-index and observe that \[ \Pi_k(V)=\bigcup_{\gamma\in\NN_D^k}\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V) \] where \[ \Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)=\big\{p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}:\ \text{$p_l\in V$ are distinct for all $1\le l\le k$} \big\}. \] Since there are $D^k$ possible choices of exponents $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k\in\NN_D$ when $k\in\NN_D$, it only suffices to prove that every $\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$ can be partitioned into a union (not necessarily disjoint) of at most $C_k\log N$ sets with $\mathcal O$ property.
nodes.statement_short: Fix the exponent multi-index $\gamma$ and reduce the lemma to a partition statement for each $\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$.

nodes.name: Claim: a small family of separating partitions of $V$
nodes.statement: We claim that for each $k\in\NN$ there is a constant $C_k>0$ and a family \begin{align} \pi=\big\{\pi_i(V): 1\le i\le C_k\log |V|\big\} \end{align} of partitions of $V$ such that \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] for every $1\le i\le C_k\log |V|$ each $\pi_i(V)=\{V_1^i,\ldots, V_k^i\}$ consists of pairwise disjoint subsets of $V$ and $V=V_1^i\cup\ldots\cup V_k^i$; \item[(ii)] for every $E\subseteq V$ with at least $k$ elements there exists $\pi_i(V)=\{V_1^i,\ldots, V_k^i\}\in\pi$ such that $E\cap V_j^i\not=\emptyset$ for every $1\le j\le k$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: State the key combinatorial claim: $O(\log|V|)$ partitions into $k$ parts suffice to separate every $k$-element subset.

nodes.name: Deduce the $\mathcal O$-property decomposition from the family $\pi$
nodes.statement: Assume for a moment we have constructed a family $\pi$ as in \eqref{eq:11}. Then one sees that for a fixed $\gamma\in\NN_D^k$ we have \begin{align} \Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)=\bigcup_{1\le i\le C_{k}\log |V|}\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V) \end{align} where \[ \Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)=\big\{p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}: p_{j}^{\gamma_j}\in \big(V\cap V_j^i)^{\gamma_j} \text{ and $V_j^i\in\pi_i(V)$ for each $1\le j\le k$}\big\} \] and $\big(V\cap V_j^i)^{\gamma_j}=\{p^{\gamma_j}: p\in V\cap V_j^i\} $. Indeed, the sum on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:28} is contained in $\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$ since each $\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)$ is. For the opposite inclusion take $p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}\in\Pi_k^{\gamma}(V)$ and let $E=\{p_1,\ldots, p_k\}$, then property (ii) for the family \eqref{eq:11} ensures that there is $\pi_i(V)=\{V_1^i,\ldots, V_k^i\}\in\pi$ such that $E\cap V_j^i\not=\emptyset$ for every $1\le j\le k$. Therefore, $p_{1}^{\gamma_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot p_{k}^{\gamma_k}\in\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)$. Furthermore, we see that for each $1\le i\le C_k\log N$ the sets $\Pi_{k, i}^{\gamma}(V)$ have $\mathcal O$ property.
nodes.statement_short: Granting the claim, verify both inclusions and check each resulting piece has the $\mathcal O$ property.

nodes.name: Reformulate partitions as surjections $\NN_N\mapsto\NN_k$
nodes.statement: The proof will be completed if we construct the family $\pi$ as in \eqref{eq:11} for the set $V$. We assume, for simplicity, that $V=\NN_N$ but the result is true for all $V\subseteq \NN_N$ containing at least $k$ elements. Now it will be more comfortable to work with surjective mappings $f:\NN_N\mapsto\NN_k$ rather than with partitions of $\NN_N$ into $k$ non-empty subsets. It will cause no changes to us, since every surjection $f:\NN_N\mapsto\NN_k$ determines a partition $\{f^{-1}[\{m\}]: 1\le m\le k\}$ of $\NN_N$ into $k$ non-empty subsets.
nodes.statement_short: Replace partitions by surjections $f:\NN_N\to\NN_k$.

nodes.name: Probabilistic model of random surjections
nodes.statement: For the proof we employ a probabilistic argument. Indeed, let $f:\NN_N\mapsto \NN_k$ be a random surjective mapping. Assume that for every $n\in\NN_N$ and $m\in\NN_k$ we have $\mathds{P}(\{f(n)=m\})=1/k$ independently of all other $n\in\NN_N$. For every $E\subseteq\NN_N$ with $k$ elements we have $\mathds P(\{|f[E]|=k\})=k!/k^k$. It suffices to show that for some $r\simeq_k\log N$ and $f_1, \ldots, f_r$ random surjections we have \[ \mathds P(\{\forall_{E\subseteq\NN_N}\ |E|=k\ \exists _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|=k\})>0. \] In other words, for each $E\subseteq\NN_N$ with cardinality $k$ it is always possible to find, with a positive probability, among at most $C_k\log N$ random surjections at least one $f:\NN_N\mapsto \NN_k$ such that $|f[E]|=k$. Then the set $\{f^{-1}[\{m\}]: 1\le m\le k\}$ is a partition of $\NN_N$ and $E\cap f^{-1}[\{m\}]\not=\emptyset$ for every $1\le m\le k$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce i.i.d. uniform random maps and reduce the claim to positivity of a probability.

nodes.name: Union bound on the failure probability
nodes.statement: The task now is the determine the exact value of $r\simeq_k\log N$. Take now $1\le r\le N$ independent random surjections $f_1, \ldots, f_r$ and observe that \begin{multline*} \mathds P(\{\exists_{E\subseteq\NN_N}\ |E|=k\ \forall _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|<k\})\le \sum_{E\subseteq \NN_N:\: |E|=k} \mathds P(\{\forall _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|<k\}) \\ =\sum_{E\subseteq \NN_N:\: |E|=k}\bigg(1-\frac{k!}{k^k}\bigg)^r=\binom{N}{k}\bigg(1-\frac{k!}{k^k}\bigg)^r \le\bigg(\frac{eN}{k}\bigg)^ke^{-r\frac{k!}{k^k}} =e^{k\log(\frac{eN}{k})-r\frac{k!}{k^k}}. \end{multline*} Therefore \[ \mathds P(\{\exists_{E\subseteq\NN_N}\ |E|=k\ \forall _{1\le l\le r}\ |f_l[E]|<k\})<1 \] if and only if \[ r>\frac{k^{k+1}}{k!}\log\bigg(\frac{eN}{k}\bigg). \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound the failure probability by $\binom{N}{k}(1-k!/k^k)^r$ and solve for $r$.

nodes.name: Choose $r$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Thus taking \[ r=\bigg\lceil\frac{k^{k+1}}{k!}\log\bigg(\frac{eN}{k}\bigg)\bigg\rceil+1\simeq C_k\log N \] we see that it does the job. This completes the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:12}.
nodes.statement_short: Take $r\simeq C_k\log N$ and conclude the lemma.

nodes.name: Restricted multipliers $\Delta_N^i$
nodes.statement: Now we can write \begin{align*} \Delta_N=\sum_{1\le i\le C_{\rho}\log N}\Delta_N^i \end{align*} where for each $1\le i\le C_{\rho}\log N$ \begin{align} \Delta_N^i(\xi) =\sum_{a/q \in\mathscr{U}_N^i} \Theta(\xi - a/q) \eta_N(\xi - a/q) \end{align} with $\mathscr{U}_N^i$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:12}.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Reduction of Theorem 1 to the uniform bound for $\Delta_N^i$
nodes.statement: The proof of Theorem \ref{th:3} will be completed if we show that for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ and $\rho>0$, there is a constant $C>0$ such that for any $N\in\NN$ and $1\le i\le C_{\rho} \log N$ we have \begin{align} \big\lVert \calF^{-1}\big(\Delta_N^{i} \hat{f}\big)\big\rVert_{\ell^{p}} \leq C (\boldA_p+1) \vnorm{f}_{\ell^{p}} \end{align} for every $f\in\ell^p\big(\ZZ^d\big)$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1 follows from a bound for each restricted multiplier $\Delta_N^i$ that is uniform in $i$ and $N$.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Sets $\mathscr{U}_N^\Lambda$, $\mathscr{W}_N$ and multiplier $\Delta_N^\Lambda$
nodes.statement: Let \begin{align} \Lambda \subseteq \Pi(\mathbb P_N)\cup\{1\} \end{align} be a set with $\mathcal O$ property, see Definition \ref{def:1}. Define \[ \mathscr{U}_N^\Lambda=\mathcal R\big(\big\{q=Q\cdot w: Q|Q_0\ \text{and}\ w\in \Lambda\big\}\big) \] and $\mathscr{W}_N =\mathcal R(\Lambda)$, and we introduce \begin{align} \Delta_N^\Lambda(\xi) =\sum_{a/q \in\mathscr{U}_N^\Lambda} \Theta(\xi - a/q) \eta_N(\xi - a/q). \end{align}
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Reduction to the $\Lambda$-restricted bound for $p=2r$
nodes.statement: We show that for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ and $\rho>0$, there is a constant $C>0$ such that for any $N\ge 8^{\max\{p, p'\}/\rho}$ and for any set $\Lambda$ as in \eqref{eq:300} and for every $f\in\ell^p\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \big\lVert \calF^{-1}\big(\Delta_N^{\Lambda} \hat{f}\big)\big\rVert_{\ell^{p}} \leq C (\boldA_p+1) \vnorm{f}_{\ell^{p}}. \end{align} For $N \le 8^{\max\{p, p'\}/\rho}$ the bound in \eqref{eq:302} is obvious, since we allow the constant $C>0$ to depend on $p$ and $\rho$. Moreover, by the duality and interpolation, it suffices to prove \eqref{eq:302} for $p=2r$ where $r\in\NN$. If $\Lambda=\Lambda_i(P_N)$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:12} for some $1\le i\le C_{\rho}\log N$, then we see that $\mathscr{U}_N^\Lambda=\mathscr{U}_N^i$ and $\Delta_N^{\Lambda}=\Delta_N^i$, and consequently \eqref{eq:302} implies \eqref{eq:17} as desired.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to bound $\Delta_N^{\Lambda}$ for large $N$ and even exponents $p=2r$; this implies the required bound for $\Delta_N^i$.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Coprime splitting of rationals (Chinese remainder identity)
nodes.statement: where we have used the fact, that if $(q_1, q_2)=1$ then for every $a\in\ZZ^d$, there are unique $a_1, a_2\in\ZZ^d$, such that $a_1/q_1, a_2/q_2\in[0, 1)^d$ and \begin{align} \frac{a}{q_1q_2}=\frac{a_1}{q_1}+\frac{a_2}{q_2} \pmod{\ZZ^d}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: A rational with coprime denominators splits uniquely as a sum of rationals with those denominators.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates
conclusions: there are unique $a_1, a_2\in\ZZ^d$, such that $a_1/q_1, a_2/q_2\in[0, 1)^d$ and $\frac{a}{q_1q_2}=\frac{a_1}{q_1}+\frac{a_2}{q_2} \pmod{\ZZ^d}$

nodes.name: Periodic splitting of $\Delta_N^{\Lambda}$ over $b\in\NN_{Q_0}^d$
nodes.statement: The function $\Theta(\xi)\eta_N(\xi)$ is regarded as a periodic function on $\TT^d$, thus \begin{align*} \Delta_N^{\Lambda}(\xi)&=\sum_{a/q\in \mathscr{U}_N^\Lambda}\Theta(\xi-a/q)\eta_N(\xi-a/q)\\ &= \sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}^d}\sum_{a/w\in \mathscr{W}_N}\Theta(\xi-b/Q_0-a/w)\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-a/w) \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Separate the $Q_0$-part $b/Q_0$ from the $\Lambda$-part $a/w$ in the sum defining $\Delta_N^{\Lambda}$.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Rational families $\mathcal U_{\{j\}}$, $\mathcal U_M$ and $\mathcal V_M^{\sigma}$
nodes.statement: Since $\Lambda$ has $\mathcal O$ property then according to Definition \ref{def:1} there is an integer $1\le k\le 2/\rho+1$ and there are sets $S_1, \ldots, S_k$ such that for any $j\in\NN_k$ we have $S_j=\{q_{j, 1},\ldots,q_{j, \beta_j} \}$ for some $\beta_j\in\NN$. Now for each $j\in\NN_k$ we introduce \[ \mathcal U_{\{j\}}=\big\{a_{j, s}/q_{j, s}\in\TT^d\cap \QQ^d: s\in\NN_{\beta_j}\ \text{and}\ a_{j, s}\in A_{q_{j, s}}\big\} \] and for any $M=\{j_1, \ldots, j_m\}\subseteq \NN_k$ let \[ \mathcal U_M=\big\{u_{j_1}+\ldots+u_{j_m}\in\TT^d\cap \QQ^d: u_{j_l}\in \mathcal U_{\{j_l\}}\ \text{for any}\ l\in\NN_m\big\}. \] For any sequence $\sigma=(s_{j_1}, \ldots, s_{j_m})\in \NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_m}}$ determined by the set $M$, let us define \[ \mathcal V_M^{\sigma}=\big\{a_{j_1, s_{j_1}}/q_{j_1, s_{j_1}}+\ldots+ a_{j_m, s_{j_m}}/q_{j_m, s_{j_m}}\in\TT^d\cap \QQ^d: a_{j_l, s_{j_l}}\in A_{q_{j_l, s_{j_l}}}\ \text{for any}\ l\in\NN_m\big\}. \] Note that $\mathcal V_M^{\sigma}$ is a subset of $\mathcal U_M$ with fixed denominators $q_{j_1, s_{j_1}},\ldots,q_{j_m, s_{j_m}}$. If $M=\emptyset$ then we have $\mathcal U_M=\mathcal V_M=\{0\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the rationals of $\mathscr W_N$ into coordinate families indexed by subsets $M\subseteq\NN_k$, with $\mathcal V_M^\sigma\subseteq\mathcal U_M$ having fixed denominators.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Multipliers $m_u$ and the decomposition of $\Delta_N^\Lambda$
nodes.statement: Let \[ \chi(\xi)=\ind{\Lambda}(\xi) \qquad \text{and} \qquad \Omega_N(\xi)=\Theta(\xi)\eta_N(\xi). \] Then again by \eqref{eq:343} we obtain \begin{multline} \Delta_N^\Lambda(\xi)= \sum_{a/w\in \mathscr{W}_N}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}^d}\Theta(\xi-b/Q_0-a/w)\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-a/w)\\ =\sum_{s_1\in\NN_{\beta_1}}\sum_{a_{1, s_1}\in A_{q_{1, s_1}}}\ldots\sum_{s_k\in\NN_{\beta_k}} \sum_{a_{k, s_k}\in A_{q_{k, s_k}}} m_{a_{1, s_1}/q_{1, s_1}+\ldots+a_{k, s_k}/q_{k, s_k} }(\xi)=\sum_{u\in \mathcal U_{\NN_k}}m_{u}(\xi) \end{multline} where \begin{align} m_{u}(\xi)=m_{a_{1, s_1}/q_{1, s_1}+\ldots+a_{k, s_k}/q_{k, s_k} }(\xi)=\chi(q_{1, s_1}\cdot\ldots\cdot q_{k, s_k})\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}^d} \Omega_N\Big(\xi-b/Q_0-\sum_{j=1}^ka_{j, s_j}/q_{j, s_j}\Big) \end{align} for $u= a_{1, s_1}/q_{1, s_1}+\ldots+a_{k, s_k}/q_{k, s_k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $\Delta_N^\Lambda=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}}m_u$, where $m_u$ is the $Q_0$-periodization of $\Omega_N$ centred at $u$.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: The pieces $f_u=\mathcal F^{-1}(m_u\hat f)$
nodes.statement: From now on we will write, for every $u\in \mathcal U_{\NN_k}$, that \begin{align} f_u(x)=\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_u\hat{f}\big)(x) \end{align} with $f\in\ell^{2r}\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ and $r\in\NN$. Therefore, \begin{align} \mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_N^{\Lambda}\hat{f}\big)(x)=\sum_{u\in \mathcal U_{\NN_k}}f_u(x) \end{align}
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Theorem 2 ($\ell^{2r}$ bound for $\sum_u f_u$)
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\rho>0$ and $r\in\NN$ are given. Then there is a constant $C_{\rho, r}>0$ such that for any $N>8^{2r/\rho}$ and for any set $\Lambda$ as in \eqref{eq:300} and for every $f\in\ell^{2r}\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \Big\|\sum_{u\in \mathcal U_{\NN_k}}f_u\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}\le C_{\rho, r}\|f\|_{\ell^{2r}}. \end{align} Moreover, the integer $k\in\NN_D$, the set $\mathcal U_{\NN_k}$ and consequently the sets $S_1,\ldots, S_k$ are determined by the set $\Lambda$ as it was described above.
nodes.statement_short: The full sum $\sum_{u}f_u$ is bounded on $\ell^{2r}$ with a constant independent of $N$ and $\Lambda$.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Square function $\mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}$
nodes.statement: Let us introduce a suitable square function which will be useful in bounding \eqref{eq:677}. For any $M\subseteq \NN_k$ and $L=\{j_1, \ldots, j_l\}\subseteq M$ and any sequence $\sigma=(s_{j_1},\ldots,s_{j_l})\in \NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_l}}$ determined by the set $L$ let us define the following square function $\mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)$ associated with the sequence $\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)$ of complex-valued functions as in \eqref{eq:25}, by setting \begin{align} \mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u(x):u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)=\bigg( \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{M\setminus L}}\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{L}^{\sigma}}f_{w+u+v}(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^{1/2}, \end{align} where $M^c=\NN_k\setminus M$.
nodes.statement_short: An $\ell^2$ square function over $w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}$ of subsums of $(f_u)$ with the $L$-coordinates frozen by $\sigma$.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates
nodes.genus: square function associated with the sequence $\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)$ of complex-valued functions
differentia: $\mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u(x):u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)=\bigg( \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{M\setminus L}}\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{L}^{\sigma}}f_{w+u+v}(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^{1/2}$

nodes.name: Mixed norm $\|\cdot\|_{\ell^2_{s_{j_i}}}$ of the square function
nodes.statement: For some $s_{j_i}\in\{s_{j_1}, \ldots, s_{j_l}\}$ we will write \begin{align*} \big\|\mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u(x):u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2_{s_{j_i}}}=\bigg(\sum_{s_{j_i}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_i}}} \big|\mathcal S_{L, M}^{(s_{j_1},\ldots,s_{j_l})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)(x)\big|^2\bigg)^{1/2} \end{align*} which defines some function which depends on $x\in\ZZ^d$ and on each $s_{j_n}\in \{s_{j_1}, \ldots, s_{j_l}\}\setminus\{s_{j_i}\}$.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Orthogonality heuristic behind the square function
nodes.statement: For the proof of \eqref{eq:677} we have to exploit the fact that the Fourier transform of $f_u$ is defined as a sum of disjointly supported smooth cut-off functions. Then appropriate subsums of $\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}}f_u$ should be strongly orthogonal to each other.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Theorem 3 (square function domination of $\sum_u f_u$)
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\rho>0$ and $r\in\NN$ are given. Then there is a constant $C_{\rho, r}>0$ such that for any $N>8^{2r/\rho}$ and for any set $\Lambda$ as in \eqref{eq:300} and for every $f\in\ell^{2r}\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \Big\|\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}} f_{u}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} \le C_{\rho, r}\sum_{\atop{M\subseteq \NN_k}{M=\{j_1, \ldots, j_m\}}}\sum_{\sigma\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_m}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{M, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}. \end{align} Moreover, the integer $k\in\NN_D$, the set $\mathcal U_{\NN_k}$ and consequently the sets $S_1,\ldots, S_k$ are determined by the set $\Lambda$ as it was described above the formulation of Theorem \ref{thm:500}.
nodes.statement_short: The $\ell^{2r}$ norm of $\sum_u f_u$ is dominated by a sum of square functions $\mathcal S_{M,M}^{\sigma}$ over all $M$ and $\sigma$.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates
conclusions: $\Big\|\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}} f_{u}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} \le C_{\rho, r}\sum_{M\subseteq \NN_k}\sum_{\sigma} \big\|\mathcal S_{M, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}$

nodes.name: Recursive square function inequalities from Mirek-Stein-Trojan
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm:500}, there is a constant $C_r>0$ such that for any $M\subseteq\NN_k$ and $L=\{j_1,\ldots, j_l\}\subseteq M$ and $j_n\in M\setminus L$ and for any $\sigma=(s_{j_1}, \ldots, s_{j_l})\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_l}}$ determined by the set $L$ we have \begin{align} \big\| \mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}\le C_r\Big\|\big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2_{s_{j_n}}}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}} \end{align} where $\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}=(s_{j_1},\ldots,s_{j_l}, s_{j_n})\in \NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_l}}\times\NN_{\beta_{j_n}}$ is the sequence determined by the set $L\cup\{s_{j_n}\}$. Moreover, the right-hand side in \eqref{eq:119} can be controlled in the following way \begin{multline} \Big\|\big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2_{ s_{j_n}}}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} \le C_r\sum_{s_{j_n}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_n}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ +C_r\big\|\mathcal S_{L, M\setminus\{j_n\}}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}. \end{multline} The proof of \eqref{eq:119} and \eqref{eq:129} can be found in \cite{mst1}.
nodes.statement_short: Adding one index to $L$ costs only a constant, and the resulting mixed norm splits into a sum over the new index plus a square function with $M$ shrunk.

nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm:500}, there exists a constant $C_{\rho, r}>0$ such that for any $M=\{j_1,\ldots, j_m\}\subseteq\NN_{k}$ any $\sigma=(s_{j_1},\ldots, s_{j_m})\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_m}}$ determined by the set $M$ and $f\in\ell^{2r}\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ we have \begin{equation} \big\|\mathcal S_{M, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}} \le C_{\rho, r} \mathbf A_r \Big\|\mathcal S_{M, M}^{\sigma}\Big(\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-u)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big):u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm:500}, there is a constant $C_r>0$ such that for any $M\subseteq\NN_k$ and $L=\{j_1,\ldots, j_l\}\subseteq M$ and $j_n\in M\setminus L$ and for any $\sigma=(s_{j_1}, \ldots, s_{j_l})\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_l}}$ determined by the set $L$ we have \begin{align} \big\| \mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}\le C_r\Big\|\big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2_{s_{j_n}}}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}} \end{align} where $\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}=(s_{j_1},\ldots,s_{j_l}, s_{j_n})\in \NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_l}}\times\NN_{\beta_{j_n}}$ is the sequence determined by the set $L\cup\{s_{j_n}\}$. Moreover, the right-hand side in \eqref{eq:119} can be controlled in the following way \begin{multline} \Big\|\big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2_{ s_{j_n}}}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} \le C_r\sum_{s_{j_n}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_n}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ +C_r\big\|\mathcal S_{L, M\setminus\{j_n\}}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}. \end{multline} The proof of \eqref{eq:119} and \eqref{eq:129} can be found in \cite{mst1}. Therefore, \eqref{eq:119} combined with \eqref{eq:129} yields \begin{align} \begin{split} \big\| \mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}&\le C_r\sum_{s_{j_n}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_n}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ &+C_r\big\|\mathcal S_{L, M\setminus\{j_n\}}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}. \end{split} \end{align} Applying \eqref{eq:1190} recursively we obtain \begin{multline} \Big\|\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}} f_{u}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}=\big\|\mathcal S_{\emptyset, \NN_k}\big(f_u: u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ \lesssim _r \sum_{s_{k}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_k}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k\}, \NN_k}^{(s_{k})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} +\big\|\mathcal S_{\emptyset, \NN_{k-1}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ \lesssim_r \sum_{s_{k-1}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_{k-1}}}}\sum_{s_{k}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_k}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k-1, k\}, \NN_k}^{(s_{k-1}, s_{k})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}+ \sum_{s_{k}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_k}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k\}, \NN_{k}\setminus\{k-1\}}^{(s_{k})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ +\sum_{s_{k-1}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_{k-1}}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k-1\}, \NN_{k-1}}^{(s_{k-1})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} +\big\|\mathcal S_{\emptyset, \NN_{k-2}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ \lesssim_r\ldots\lesssim_{\rho, r}\sum_{\atop{M\subseteq \NN_k}{M=\{j_1, \ldots, j_m\}}}\sum_{\sigma\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_m}}} \sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}f_{w+v}(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r. \end{multline} The proof of \eqref{eq:130} is completed.
nodes.statement_short: Iterate the two inequalities (119) and (129) of [mst1] one index at a time, peeling off the coordinates of $\NN_k$ until only the terms $\mathcal S_{M,M}^{\sigma}$ remain.

nodes.name: Invoke the two cited square function inequalities
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm:500}, there is a constant $C_r>0$ such that for any $M\subseteq\NN_k$ and $L=\{j_1,\ldots, j_l\}\subseteq M$ and $j_n\in M\setminus L$ and for any $\sigma=(s_{j_1}, \ldots, s_{j_l})\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_l}}$ determined by the set $L$ we have \begin{align} \big\| \mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}\le C_r\Big\|\big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2_{s_{j_n}}}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}} \end{align} where $\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}=(s_{j_1},\ldots,s_{j_l}, s_{j_n})\in \NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_l}}\times\NN_{\beta_{j_n}}$ is the sequence determined by the set $L\cup\{s_{j_n}\}$. Moreover, the right-hand side in \eqref{eq:119} can be controlled in the following way \begin{multline} \Big\|\big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2_{ s_{j_n}}}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} \le C_r\sum_{s_{j_n}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_n}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ +C_r\big\|\mathcal S_{L, M\setminus\{j_n\}}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}. \end{multline} The proof of \eqref{eq:119} and \eqref{eq:129} can be found in \cite{mst1}.
nodes.statement_short: Quote inequalities (119) and (129) proved in [mst1].

nodes.name: Combine (119) and (129) into the one-step recursion
nodes.statement: Therefore, \eqref{eq:119} combined with \eqref{eq:129} yields \begin{align} \begin{split} \big\| \mathcal S_{L, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}&\le C_r\sum_{s_{j_n}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_n}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{L\cup\{j_n\}, M}^{\sigma\oplus s_{j_n}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ &+C_r\big\|\mathcal S_{L, M\setminus\{j_n\}}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}. \end{split} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Chain the two inequalities to obtain the single recursion step (1190).
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Iterate the recursion and conclude
nodes.statement: Applying \eqref{eq:1190} recursively we obtain \begin{multline} \Big\|\sum_{u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}} f_{u}\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}=\big\|\mathcal S_{\emptyset, \NN_k}\big(f_u: u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ \lesssim _r \sum_{s_{k}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_k}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k\}, \NN_k}^{(s_{k})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} +\big\|\mathcal S_{\emptyset, \NN_{k-1}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ \lesssim_r \sum_{s_{k-1}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_{k-1}}}}\sum_{s_{k}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_k}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k-1, k\}, \NN_k}^{(s_{k-1}, s_{k})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}+ \sum_{s_{k}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_k}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k\}, \NN_{k}\setminus\{k-1\}}^{(s_{k})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ +\sum_{s_{k-1}\in\NN_{\beta_{j_{k-1}}}} \big\|\mathcal S_{\{k-1\}, \NN_{k-1}}^{(s_{k-1})}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r} +\big\|\mathcal S_{\emptyset, \NN_{k-2}}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big) \big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\\ \lesssim_r\ldots\lesssim_{\rho, r}\sum_{\atop{M\subseteq \NN_k}{M=\{j_1, \ldots, j_m\}}}\sum_{\sigma\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_m}}} \sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}f_{w+v}(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r. \end{multline} The proof of \eqref{eq:130} is completed.
nodes.statement_short: Peel off the indices $k, k-1,\ldots$ one at a time to reach the full sum over $M$ and $\sigma$.
nodes.section: Further reductions and square function estimates

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.2
nodes.statement: We assume, without of loss of generality, that $N\in\NN$ is large. Let $B_h=q_{j_1, s_{j_1}}\cdot\ldots\cdot q_{j_m, s_{j_m}}\cdot Q_0\le e^{N^{\rho}}$ and observe that according to the notation from \eqref{eq:25} and \eqref{eq:13}, we have \begin{multline} \big\|\mathcal S_{M, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}= \sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}f_{w+v}(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r\\ \le\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\calF^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\Theta(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r\\ =\sum_{n\in \NN_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\big|\calF^{-1}\big(\Theta\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big|^2\bigg)^r \end{multline} where \begin{align} G(\xi; n, w)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}^d}\hat{f}(\xi+b/Q_0+v+w)e^{-2\pi i (b/Q_0+v)\cdot n}. \end{align} We know that for each $0<p<\infty$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that for any $d\in\NN$ and $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d\in\CC^d$ we have \begin{align} \bigg(\int_{\CC^d}|\lambda_1z_1+\ldots+\lambda_dz_d|^pe^{-\pi |z|^2} {\rm d} z\bigg)^{1/p}=C_p\big(|\lambda_1|^2+\ldots+|\lambda_d|^2\big)^{1/2}. \end{align} By Proposition 4.5 from \cite{mst1}, with the sequence of multipliers $\Theta_N=\Theta$ for all $N\in\NN$ and $\Theta$ as in \eqref{eq:155}, we have \begin{align} \big\|\calF^{-1}\big(\Theta\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}(x)}\le C_{\rho, r}\mathbf A_{2r} \big\|\calF^{-1}\big(\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}(x)} \end{align} since $\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\varepsilon_{\gamma}^{-1}\ge e^{N^{2\rho}}\ge 2e^{(d+1)N^{\rho}}\ge B_h$ for sufficiently large $N\in\NN$. Therefore, combining \eqref{eq:140} with \eqref{eq:1411} we obtain that \begin{multline} \sum_{n\in \NN_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\big|\calF^{-1}\big(\Theta\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big|^2\bigg)^r \\=C_{2r}^{2r}\int_{\CC^d} \sum_{n\in \NN_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\Big|\calF^{-1}\Big(\Theta\eta_N\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}z_{w} G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\Big)\Big)(B_hx+n)\Big|^{2r}e^{-\pi |z|^2}{\rm d}z\\ \lesssim_r\int_{\CC^d} \sum_{n\in \NN_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\Big|\calF^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}z_{w} \eta_NG(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\Big)(B_hx+n)\Big|^{2r}e^{-\pi |z|^2}{\rm d}z\\ \lesssim_r\sum_{n\in \NN_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\big|\calF^{-1}\big(\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big|^2\bigg)^r\\ \lesssim_r\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\calF^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r. \end{multline} This completes the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:5}.
nodes.statement_short: Split $\ZZ^d$ into residue classes modulo $B_h$, linearise the square function by the complex Gaussian identity, and transfer $\Theta$ away using Proposition 4.5 of [mst1].

nodes.name: Split into residue classes modulo $B_h$
nodes.statement: We assume, without of loss of generality, that $N\in\NN$ is large. Let $B_h=q_{j_1, s_{j_1}}\cdot\ldots\cdot q_{j_m, s_{j_m}}\cdot Q_0\le e^{N^{\rho}}$ and observe that according to the notation from \eqref{eq:25} and \eqref{eq:13}, we have \begin{multline} \big\|\mathcal S_{M, M}^{\sigma}\big(f_u:u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\big)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}= \sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}f_{w+v}(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r\\ \le\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\calF^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\Theta(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r\\ =\sum_{n\in \NN_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\big|\calF^{-1}\big(\Theta\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big|^2\bigg)^r \end{multline} where \begin{align} G(\xi; n, w)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}^d}\hat{f}(\xi+b/Q_0+v+w)e^{-2\pi i (b/Q_0+v)\cdot n}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the square function as a sum over residue classes $B_hx+n$ with the auxiliary function $G(\xi;n,w)$.

nodes.name: Complex Gaussian linearisation identity
nodes.statement: We know that for each $0<p<\infty$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that for any $d\in\NN$ and $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d\in\CC^d$ we have \begin{align} \bigg(\int_{\CC^d}|\lambda_1z_1+\ldots+\lambda_dz_d|^pe^{-\pi |z|^2} {\rm d} z\bigg)^{1/p}=C_p\big(|\lambda_1|^2+\ldots+|\lambda_d|^2\big)^{1/2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Recall the Gaussian identity turning an $\ell^2$ sum into an $L^p$ average of linear combinations.
nodes.section: Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 4.5 of [mst1] to remove $\Theta$
nodes.statement: By Proposition 4.5 from \cite{mst1}, with the sequence of multipliers $\Theta_N=\Theta$ for all $N\in\NN$ and $\Theta$ as in \eqref{eq:155}, we have \begin{align} \big\|\calF^{-1}\big(\Theta\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}(x)}\le C_{\rho, r}\mathbf A_{2r} \big\|\calF^{-1}\big(\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big\|_{\ell^{2r}(x)} \end{align} since $\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\varepsilon_{\gamma}^{-1}\ge e^{N^{2\rho}}\ge 2e^{(d+1)N^{\rho}}\ge B_h$ for sufficiently large $N\in\NN$.
nodes.statement_short: Transfer the continuous multiplier bound to the sampled lattice $B_h\ZZ^d+n$.

nodes.name: Combine and conclude
nodes.statement: Therefore, combining \eqref{eq:140} with \eqref{eq:1411} we obtain that \begin{multline} \sum_{n\in \NN_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\big|\calF^{-1}\big(\Theta\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big|^2\bigg)^r \\=C_{2r}^{2r}\int_{\CC^d} \sum_{n\in \NN_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\Big|\calF^{-1}\Big(\Theta\eta_N\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}z_{w} G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\Big)\Big)(B_hx+n)\Big|^{2r}e^{-\pi |z|^2}{\rm d}z\\ \lesssim_r\int_{\CC^d} \sum_{n\in \NN_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\Big|\calF^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}z_{w} \eta_NG(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\Big)(B_hx+n)\Big|^{2r}e^{-\pi |z|^2}{\rm d}z\\ \lesssim_r\sum_{n\in \NN_{B_h}^d}\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\big|\calF^{-1}\big(\eta_N G(\: \cdot\: ;n, w)\big)(B_hx+n)\big|^2\bigg)^r\\ \lesssim_r\sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\bigg(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\calF^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\bigg)^r. \end{multline} This completes the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:5}.
nodes.statement_short: Chain the Gaussian identity with the transference bound and undo the residue-class splitting.
nodes.section: Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: It remains to show that there exists a constant $C_{\rho, r}>0$ such that for any $M=\{j_1,\ldots, j_m\}\subseteq\NN_{k}$ any $\sigma=(s_{j_1},\ldots, s_{j_m})\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_m}}$ determined by the set $M$ and $f\in\ell^{2r}\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \sum_{\sigma\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_m}}}\Big\|\mathcal S_{M, M}^{\sigma}\Big(\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-u)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big):u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\le C_{\rho, r}^{2r}\|f\|_{\ell^{2r}}. \end{align} Since there are $2^k$ possible choices of sets $M\subseteq \NN_k$ and $k\in\NN_D$ then \eqref{eq:134} will follow and the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:500} will be completed. If $r=1$ the then Plancherel's theorem does the job since the functions $\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)$ are disjointly supported for all $b/Q_0\in \NN_{Q_0}$, $w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}$, $v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}$ and $\sigma=(s_{j_1},\ldots, s_{j_m})\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_m}}$. For general $r\ge2$, since $\|f\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}=\|f\|_{\ell^{2}}^2$ because we have assumed that $f$ is a characteristic function of a finite set in $\ZZ^d$, it suffices to prove for any $x\in\ZZ^d$ that \begin{align} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\calF^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\le C_{\rho, r}. \end{align} In fact, since $\|f\|_{\ell^{\infty}}=1$, it is enough to show \begin{align} \Big\|\calF^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^1}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} for any sequence of complex numbers $\big(\alpha(w): w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}\big)$ such that \begin{align} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}|\alpha(w)|^2=1. \end{align} Computing the Fourier transform we obtain \begin{multline} \calF^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\Big)\\ =\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot w}\Big)\cdot \det(\mathcal E_N)\mathcal F^{-1}\eta\big(\mathcal E_Nx\big)\cdot\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q_0+v)}\Big). \end{multline} The function \begin{align} \sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q_0+v)} \end{align} can be written as a sum of $2^m$ functions \begin{align} \sum_{b\in\NN_{Q}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q)} = \begin{cases} Q^d & \mbox{if } x \equiv 0 \pmod{Q}, \\ 0 & \mbox{otherwise,} \end{cases} \end{align} where possible values of $Q$ are products of $Q_0$ and $p_{j_i, s_{j_i}}^{\gamma_i}$ or $p_{j_i, s_{j_i}}^{\gamma_i-1}$ for $i\in\NN_m$. Therefore, the proof of \eqref{eq:144} will be completed if we show that \begin{align} \Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot Q^d\det(\mathcal E_N)\mathcal F^{-1}\eta\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^1(x)}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} for any integer $Q\le e^{N^{\rho}}$ such that $(Q, q_{j, s})=1$, for all $j\in M^c$ and $s\in\NN_{\beta_j}$. Recall that, according Remark \ref{rem:1}, in our case $\eta=\phi*\psi$ for some two smooth functions $\phi, \psi$ supported in $(-1/(8d), 1/(8d))^d$. Therefore, by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality we only need to prove that \begin{align} Q^{d/2}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{1/2}\big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\phi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\big\|_{\ell^2(x)}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} and \begin{align} Q^{d/2}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{1/2}\Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^2(x)}\le C_{\rho, r}. \end{align} Since $(Q, q_{j, s})=1$, for all $j\in M^c$ and $s\in\NN_{\beta_j}$ then $Qw\not\in \ZZ^d$ for any $w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}$ and its denominator is bounded by $N^D$. We can assume, without of loss of generality, that $Qw\in[0, 1)^d$ by the periodicity of $x\mapsto e^{-2\pi i x\cdot Qw}$. Inequality \eqref{eq:22} easily follows from Plancherel's theorem. In order to prove \eqref{eq:15} observe that by the change of variables one has \begin{align*} \Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot Qw}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)=Q^{-d}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{-1} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\psi\big(Q^{-1}\mathcal E_N^{-1}(\: \cdot-Qw) \big)\big)(x). \end{align*} Therefore, Plancherel's theorem and the last identity yield \begin{multline} Q^{d}\det(\mathcal E_N)\Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^2(x)}^2\\= \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}|\alpha(w)|^2\int_{\RR^d}\big|\psi(\xi-\mathcal E_N^{-1}w)\big|^2{\rm d}\xi+\sum_{\atop{w_1, w_2\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}{w_1\not=w_2}}\alpha(w_1)\overline{\alpha(w_2)}\int_{\RR^d}\psi(\xi)\psi\big(\xi-\mathcal E_N^{-1}(w_1-w_2)\big){\rm d}\xi. \end{multline} The first sum on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:58} is bounded in view of \eqref{eq:50}. The second one vanishes since the function $\psi$ is supported in $(-1/(8d), 1/(8d))^d$ and $|\mathcal E_N^{-1}(w_1-w_2)|_{\infty}\ge e^{N^{2\rho}}N^{-2D}>1$, for sufficiently large $N$. The proof of Theorem \ref{thm:500} is completed.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to an $\ell^1$ kernel bound; for $r=1$ Plancherel and disjoint supports suffice, and for $r\ge2$ factor $\eta=\phi*\psi$, apply Cauchy-Schwarz and kill the cross terms by support separation.

nodes.name: State the remaining estimate (143)
nodes.statement: It remains to show that there exists a constant $C_{\rho, r}>0$ such that for any $M=\{j_1,\ldots, j_m\}\subseteq\NN_{k}$ any $\sigma=(s_{j_1},\ldots, s_{j_m})\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_m}}$ determined by the set $M$ and $f\in\ell^{2r}\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \sum_{\sigma\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_m}}}\Big\|\mathcal S_{M, M}^{\sigma}\Big(\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-u)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big):u\in\mathcal U_{\NN_k}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}\le C_{\rho, r}^{2r}\|f\|_{\ell^{2r}}. \end{align} Since there are $2^k$ possible choices of sets $M\subseteq \NN_k$ and $k\in\NN_D$ then \eqref{eq:134} will follow and the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:500} will be completed.
nodes.statement_short: Isolate the remaining bound (143), summable over the $2^k$ choices of $M$.

nodes.name: Case $r=1$: Plancherel and disjoint supports
nodes.statement: If $r=1$ the then Plancherel's theorem does the job since the functions $\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)$ are disjointly supported for all $b/Q_0\in \NN_{Q_0}$, $w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}$, $v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}$ and $\sigma=(s_{j_1},\ldots, s_{j_m})\in\NN_{\beta_{j_1}}\times\ldots\times\NN_{\beta_{j_m}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Dispose of the case $r=1$ by Plancherel plus disjointness of the cut-off supports.

nodes.name: Case $r\ge2$: reduce to a pointwise bound
nodes.statement: For general $r\ge2$, since $\|f\|_{\ell^{2r}}^{2r}=\|f\|_{\ell^{2}}^2$ because we have assumed that $f$ is a characteristic function of a finite set in $\ZZ^d$, it suffices to prove for any $x\in\ZZ^d$ that \begin{align} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\Big|\calF^{-1}\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\hat{f}(\xi)\Big)(x)\Big|^2\le C_{\rho, r}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: For $r\ge2$ use that $f$ is an indicator to reduce to a uniform pointwise square-sum bound.
