nodes.name: Dualize to an $\ell^1$ kernel bound
nodes.statement: In fact, since $\|f\|_{\ell^{\infty}}=1$, it is enough to show \begin{align} \Big\|\calF^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^1}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} for any sequence of complex numbers $\big(\alpha(w): w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}\big)$ such that \begin{align} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}|\alpha(w)|^2=1. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Replace the pointwise bound by a uniform $\ell^1$ bound on the randomized kernel.
nodes.section: Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Compute the Fourier transform and the root-of-unity sum
nodes.statement: Computing the Fourier transform we obtain \begin{multline} \calF^{-1}\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}\eta_N(\xi-b/Q_0-v-w)\Big)\\ =\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot w}\Big)\cdot \det(\mathcal E_N)\mathcal F^{-1}\eta\big(\mathcal E_Nx\big)\cdot\Big(\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q_0+v)}\Big). \end{multline} The function \begin{align} \sum_{v\in\mathcal V_{M}^{\sigma}}\sum_{b\in\NN_{Q_0}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q_0+v)} \end{align} can be written as a sum of $2^m$ functions \begin{align} \sum_{b\in\NN_{Q}}e^{-2\pi i x\cdot (b/Q)} = \begin{cases} Q^d & \mbox{if } x \equiv 0 \pmod{Q}, \\ 0 & \mbox{otherwise,} \end{cases} \end{align} where possible values of $Q$ are products of $Q_0$ and $p_{j_i, s_{j_i}}^{\gamma_i}$ or $p_{j_i, s_{j_i}}^{\gamma_i-1}$ for $i\in\NN_m$.
nodes.statement_short: Factor the kernel into an exponential sum, a rescaled $\mathcal F^{-1}\eta$, and a complete root-of-unity sum supported on $Q\ZZ^d$.
nodes.section: Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Split by Cauchy-Schwarz using $\eta=\phi*\psi$
nodes.statement: Therefore, the proof of \eqref{eq:144} will be completed if we show that \begin{align} \Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot Q^d\det(\mathcal E_N)\mathcal F^{-1}\eta\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^1(x)}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} for any integer $Q\le e^{N^{\rho}}$ such that $(Q, q_{j, s})=1$, for all $j\in M^c$ and $s\in\NN_{\beta_j}$. Recall that, according Remark \ref{rem:1}, in our case $\eta=\phi*\psi$ for some two smooth functions $\phi, \psi$ supported in $(-1/(8d), 1/(8d))^d$. Therefore, by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality we only need to prove that \begin{align} Q^{d/2}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{1/2}\big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\phi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\big\|_{\ell^2(x)}\le C_{\rho, r} \end{align} and \begin{align} Q^{d/2}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{1/2}\Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^2(x)}\le C_{\rho, r}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Use the factorization $\eta=\phi*\psi$ and Cauchy-Schwarz to split the $\ell^1$ bound into two $\ell^2$ bounds.
nodes.section: Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Plancherel and vanishing of the cross terms
nodes.statement: Since $(Q, q_{j, s})=1$, for all $j\in M^c$ and $s\in\NN_{\beta_j}$ then $Qw\not\in \ZZ^d$ for any $w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}$ and its denominator is bounded by $N^D$. We can assume, without of loss of generality, that $Qw\in[0, 1)^d$ by the periodicity of $x\mapsto e^{-2\pi i x\cdot Qw}$. Inequality \eqref{eq:22} easily follows from Plancherel's theorem. In order to prove \eqref{eq:15} observe that by the change of variables one has \begin{align*} \Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot Qw}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)=Q^{-d}\det(\mathcal E_N)^{-1} \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\psi\big(Q^{-1}\mathcal E_N^{-1}(\: \cdot-Qw) \big)\big)(x). \end{align*} Therefore, Plancherel's theorem and the last identity yield \begin{multline} Q^{d}\det(\mathcal E_N)\Big\|\Big(\sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}\alpha(w)e^{-2\pi i Qx\cdot w}\Big)\cdot\mathcal F^{-1}\psi\big(Q\mathcal E_N x\big)\Big\|_{\ell^2(x)}^2\\= \sum_{w\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}|\alpha(w)|^2\int_{\RR^d}\big|\psi(\xi-\mathcal E_N^{-1}w)\big|^2{\rm d}\xi+\sum_{\atop{w_1, w_2\in\mathcal U_{M^c}}{w_1\not=w_2}}\alpha(w_1)\overline{\alpha(w_2)}\int_{\RR^d}\psi(\xi)\psi\big(\xi-\mathcal E_N^{-1}(w_1-w_2)\big){\rm d}\xi. \end{multline} The first sum on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:58} is bounded in view of \eqref{eq:50}. The second one vanishes since the function $\psi$ is supported in $(-1/(8d), 1/(8d))^d$ and $|\mathcal E_N^{-1}(w_1-w_2)|_{\infty}\ge e^{N^{2\rho}}N^{-2D}>1$, for sufficiently large $N$. The proof of Theorem \ref{thm:500} is completed.
nodes.statement_short: Expand by Plancherel: the diagonal is controlled by the normalization, the off-diagonal vanishes by support separation.
nodes.section: Concluding remarks and the proof of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Reduction of Theorem B to the dyadic sum estimate (84)
nodes.statement: This section is intended to provide the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:7}. In fact, in view of the decomposition of the kernel $K$ into dyadic pieces as in \eqref{eq:87}, instead of inequality \eqref{eq:37}, it suffices to show that for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that for all $f\in\ell^p\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \Big\|\sum_{n\in\ZZ}T_nf\Big\|_{\ell^p}\le C_p\|f\|_{\ell^p} \end{align} where \begin{align} T_n f(x) = \sum_{y\in\ZZ^k} f\big(x - \calQ(y)\big) K_n(y) \end{align} with the kernel $K_n$ as in \eqref{eq:87} for each $n\in\ZZ$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem B reduces to the uniform $\ell^p$ bound for $\sum_{n\in\ZZ}T_n$.

nodes.name: Gaussian sums $G(a/q)$
nodes.statement: Recall that for $q\in\NN$ \[ A_q=\big\{a\in\NN_q^d: \mathrm{gcd}\big(q, \mathrm(a_{\gamma}: \gamma\in\Gamma)\big)\big\}. \] Now for $q \in \NN$ and $a \in A_q$ we define the Gaussian sums $$ G(a/q) = q^{-k} \sum_{y \in \NN^k_q} e^{2\pi i \sprod{(a/q)}{\calQ(y)}}. $$

nodes.name: Power-saving bound for the Gaussian sums
nodes.statement: Let us observe that there exists $\delta>0$ such that \begin{equation} \lvert G(a/q) \rvert \lesssim q^{-\delta}. \end{equation} This follows from the multi-dimensional variant of Weyl's inequality (see \cite[Proposition 3]{SW0}).
nodes.statement_short: The complete Gaussian sums decay like $q^{-\delta}$ for some $\delta>0$.

nodes.name: Weyl sums $S_N$
nodes.statement:
Let $P$ be a polynomial in $\RR^k$ of degree $d \in\NN$ such that \[ P(x) = \sum_{0 < 
orm{\gamma} \leq d} \xi_\gamma x^\gamma. \] Given $N \geq 1$, let $\Omega_N$ be a convex set in $\RR^k$ such that \[ \Omega_N \subseteq  ig\{x \in \RR^k : 
orm{x-x_0} \leq cN  ig\} \] for some $x_0\in\RR^k$ and $c > 0$. We define the Weyl sums  egin{align} S_N = \sum_{n \in \Omega_N \cap \ZZ^k} e^{2\pi i P(n)}\varphi(n) \end{align} where $\varphi:\RR^k\mapsto \CC$ is a continuously differentiable function which for some $C>0$ satisfies  egin{align} |\varphi(x)|\le C, \qquad 	ext{and} \qquad |
abla \varphi(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Smoothly weighted multi-dimensional exponential sums of a polynomial phase over a convex set of diameter $\sim N$.

nodes.name: Refinement of the range of $q$ over Stein-Wainger
nodes.statement: In \cite{mst1} we have proven Theorem \ref{thm:3} which is a refinement of the estimates for the multi-dimensional Weyl sums $S_N$, where the limitations $N^\varepsilon \leq q \leq N^{k-\varepsilon}$ from \cite[Proposition 3]{SW0} are replaced by the weaker restrictions $(\log{N})^\beta \leq q \leq N^k(\log{N})^{-\beta}$ for appropriate $\beta$. Namely.
nodes.statement_short: The admissible range of denominators is widened from polynomial to logarithmic thresholds.

nodes.name: Theorem 4 (Weyl inequality with logarithmic decay)
nodes.statement: Assume that there is a multi-index $\gamma_0$ such that $0 < \norm{\gamma_0} \leq d$ and \[ \Big\lvert \xi_{\gamma_0} - \frac{a}{q} \Big\rvert \leq \frac{1}{q^2} \] for some integers $a, q$ such that $0\le a\le q$ and $(a, q) = 1$. Then for any $\alpha>0$ there is $\beta_{\alpha}>0$ so that, for any $\beta\ge \beta_{\alpha}$, if \begin{equation} (\log N)^\beta \leq q \leq N^{\norm{\gamma_0}} (\log N)^{-\beta} \end{equation} then there is a constant $C>0$ \begin{equation} |S_N| \leq C N^k (\log N)^{-\alpha}. \end{equation} The implied constant $C$ is independent of $N$.
nodes.statement_short: If some coefficient of the phase has a rational approximation with denominator in a logarithmic window, the Weyl sum saves an arbitrary power of $\log N$.
assumptions: there is a multi-index $\gamma_0$ such that $0 < \norm{\gamma_0} \leq d$ and $\Big\lvert \xi_{\gamma_0} - \frac{a}{q} \Big\rvert \leq \frac{1}{q^2}$ for some integers $a, q$ such that $0\le a\le q$ and $(a, q) = 1$
conclusions: The implied constant $C$ is independent of $N$

nodes.name: Multipliers $m_n$ and their continuous counterparts $\Phi_n$
nodes.statement: Let $\big(\seq{m_n}{n \geq 0}\big)$ be a sequence of multipliers on $\TT^d$, corresponding to the operators \eqref{eq:85}. Then for any finitely supported function $f:\ZZ^d\mapsto\CC$ we see that $$ T_nf(x)=\calF^{-1} \big(m_n \hat{f}\big)(x) $$ where $$ m_n(\xi) = \sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{\xi}{\calQ(y)}} K_n(y). $$ For $n \geq 0$ we set $$ \Phi_n(\xi) = \int_{\RR^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{\xi}{\calQ(y)}} K_n(y) {\rm d}y. $$
nodes.statement_short: $m_n$ is the discrete multiplier of $T_n$ and $\Phi_n$ its integral analogue.

nodes.name: van der Corput bounds for $\Phi_n$
nodes.statement: Using multi-dimensional version of van der Corput's lemma (see \cite[Propositon 2.1]{sw}) we obtain \begin{equation} \lvert \Phi_n(\xi) \rvert \lesssim \min\big\{1, \abs{2^{n A} \xi}_{\infty}^{-1/d}\big\}. \end{equation} Moreover, if $n \geq 1$ we have \begin{equation} \lvert \Phi_n(\xi) \rvert = \Big\lvert \Phi_n(\xi) - \int_{\RR^k} K_n(y) {\rm d}y \Big\rvert \lesssim \min\big\{1, \abs{2^{nA} \xi}_{\infty} \big\}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\Phi_n$ decays like $|2^{nA}\xi|_\infty^{-1/d}$ at infinity and vanishes linearly at the origin.
nodes.origin_citation: Stein & Wainger, Proposition 2.1 (van der Corput lemma)

nodes.name: Proposition 3.1 (major-arc approximation of $m_n$)
nodes.statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that for every $n\in\NN$ and for every $\xi\in [1/2, 1/2)^d$ satisfying $$ \Big\lvert \xi_\gamma - \frac{a_\gamma}{q} \Big\rvert \leq L_1^{-|\gamma|}L_2 $$ for all $\gamma \in \Gamma$, where $1\le q\le L_3\le 2^{n/2}$, $a\in A_q$, $L_1\ge 2^n$ and $L_2\ge1$ we have \begin{align} \big|m_n(\xi)-G(a/q)\Phi_{n}(\xi-a/q)\big|\le C\Big(L_32^{-n} +L_2L_32^{-n}\sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma}\big(2^n/L_1\big)^{|\gamma|}\Big)\le CL_2L_32^{-n}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: On major arcs the discrete multiplier $m_n$ is approximated by $G(a/q)\Phi_n(\xi-a/q)$ with an explicit error.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1
nodes.statement:
Let $	heta = \xi - a/q$. For any $r \in \NN_q^k$, if $y \equiv r \pmod q$ then for each $\gamma \in \Gamma$ $$ \xi_\gamma y^\gamma \equiv 	heta_\gamma y^\gamma + (a_\gamma/q) r^\gamma \pmod 1, $$ thus $$ \sprod{\xi}{\calQ(y)} \equiv \sprod{	heta}{\calQ(y)} + \sprod{(a/q)}{\calQ(r)} \pmod 1. $$ Therefore, \[ \sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{\xi}{\calQ(y)}} K_n(y) = \sum_{r \in \NN_q^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{(a/q)}{\calQ(r)}} \sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{	heta}{\calQ(qy+r)}} K_n(qy+r). \] If $2^{n-2} \leq 
orm{q y + r}, 
orm{qy} \leq 2^n$ then by the mean value theorem we obtain \[  ig\lvert \sprod{	heta}{\calQ(q y + r)} - \sprod{	heta}{\calQ(q y)}  igvert \lesssim 
orm{r} \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} \abs{	heta_\gamma} \cdot 2^{n(\abs{\gamma} - 1)} \lesssim q \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} L_1^{-\abs{\gamma}} L_2 2^{n(\abs{\gamma}-1)} \lesssim L_2L_32^{-n}\sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} ig(2^n/L_1 ig)^{\abs{\gamma}} \] and $$  ig\lvert K_n(q y + r) - K_n(q y)  igvert \lesssim 2^{-n(k+1)}L_3. $$ Thus \[ \sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{\xi}{\calQ(y)}} K_n(y) =G(a/q)\cdot q^k\sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{	heta}{\calQ(qy)}} K_n(qy) +\mathcal O\Big(L_32^{-n}+L_2L_32^{-n}\sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} ig(2^n/L_1 ig)^{|\gamma|}\Big). \] Now one can replace the sum on the right-hand side by the integral. Indeed, again by the mean value theorem we obtain  egin{multline*} \Big|\sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{	heta}{\calQ(qy)}} K_n(qy)-\int_{\RR^k}e^{2\pi i 	heta\cdot\calQ(qt)}K_n(qt){m d}t\Big|\ = \Big|\sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} \int_{[0, 1)^k} ig(e^{2\pi i \sprod{	heta}{\calQ(qy)}} K_n(qy)-e^{2\pi i 	heta\cdot\calQ(q(y+t))}K_n(q(y+t)){m d}t ig)\Big|\ =\mathcal O\Big(q^{-k}L_32^{-n}+q^{-k}L_2L_32^{-n}\sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} ig(2^n/L_1 ig)^{|\gamma|}\Big). \end{multline*} This completes the proof of Proposition ef{prop:0}.
nodes.statement_short: Split $y$ into residue classes mod $q$ to factor out the Gaussian sum, control the resulting errors by the mean value theorem, and replace the remaining sum by an integral.

nodes.name: Congruence splitting modulo $q$
nodes.statement: Let $\theta = \xi - a/q$. For any $r \in \NN_q^k$, if $y \equiv r \pmod q$ then for each $\gamma \in \Gamma$ $$ \xi_\gamma y^\gamma \equiv \theta_\gamma y^\gamma + (a_\gamma/q) r^\gamma \pmod 1, $$ thus $$ \sprod{\xi}{\calQ(y)} \equiv \sprod{\theta}{\calQ(y)} + \sprod{(a/q)}{\calQ(r)} \pmod 1. $$ Therefore, \[ \sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{\xi}{\calQ(y)}} K_n(y) = \sum_{r \in \NN_q^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{(a/q)}{\calQ(r)}} \sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{\theta}{\calQ(qy+r)}} K_n(qy+r). \]
nodes.statement_short: Write $y=qy'+r$ and separate the arithmetic phase $a/q$ from the analytic phase $\theta$.

nodes.name: Mean value theorem error estimates
nodes.statement:
If $2^{n-2} \leq 
orm{q y + r}, 
orm{qy} \leq 2^n$ then by the mean value theorem we obtain \[  ig\lvert \sprod{	heta}{\calQ(q y + r)} - \sprod{	heta}{\calQ(q y)}  igvert \lesssim 
orm{r} \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} \abs{	heta_\gamma} \cdot 2^{n(\abs{\gamma} - 1)} \lesssim q \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} L_1^{-\abs{\gamma}} L_2 2^{n(\abs{\gamma}-1)} \lesssim L_2L_32^{-n}\sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} ig(2^n/L_1 ig)^{\abs{\gamma}} \] and $$  ig\lvert K_n(q y + r) - K_n(q y)  igvert \lesssim 2^{-n(k+1)}L_3. $$
nodes.statement_short: Estimate the cost of replacing $qy+r$ by $qy$ in both the phase and the kernel.

nodes.name: Factor out the Gaussian sum
nodes.statement: Thus \[ \sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{\xi}{\calQ(y)}} K_n(y) =G(a/q)\cdot q^k\sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{\theta}{\calQ(qy)}} K_n(qy) +\mathcal O\Big(L_32^{-n}+L_2L_32^{-n}\sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma}\big(2^n/L_1\big)^{|\gamma|}\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: The arithmetic part collapses to $G(a/q)$ up to the previously estimated error.

nodes.name: Replace the sum by the integral and conclude
nodes.statement: Now one can replace the sum on the right-hand side by the integral. Indeed, again by the mean value theorem we obtain \begin{multline*} \Big|\sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} e^{2\pi i \sprod{\theta}{\calQ(qy)}} K_n(qy)-\int_{\RR^k}e^{2\pi i \theta\cdot\calQ(qt)}K_n(qt){\rm d}t\Big|\\ = \Big|\sum_{y \in \ZZ^k} \int_{[0, 1)^k}\big(e^{2\pi i \sprod{\theta}{\calQ(qy)}} K_n(qy)-e^{2\pi i \theta\cdot\calQ(q(y+t))}K_n(q(y+t)){\rm d}t\big)\Big|\\ =\mathcal O\Big(q^{-k}L_32^{-n}+q^{-k}L_2L_32^{-n}\sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma}\big(2^n/L_1\big)^{|\gamma|}\Big). \end{multline*} This completes the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:0}.
nodes.statement_short: Compare the lattice sum with its integral to produce $\Phi_n(\xi-a/q)$ and finish.

nodes.name: Multipliers $\Omega_{N}^{j, n}$
nodes.statement: Fix $j, n\in\ZZ$ and $N\in\NN$ and let $\mathcal E_N$ be a diagonal $d\times d$ matrix with positive entries $(\varepsilon_{\gamma}: \gamma\in\Gamma)$ such that $\varepsilon_{\gamma} \le e^{-N^{2\rho}}$ with $\rho>0$ as in Section \ref{sec:6}. Let us consider the multipliers \begin{align} \Omega_{N}^{j, n}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{N}}\Phi_{j, n}(\xi-a/q)\eta_N(\xi-a/q) \end{align} with $\eta_N(\xi)=\eta\big(\mathcal E_N^{-1}\xi\big)$ and $\Phi_{j, n}(\xi)=\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big)$, where $\Phi$ is a Schwartz function such that $\Phi(0)=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Arithmetic Littlewood-Paley pieces: dilated Schwartz bumps $\Phi(2^{nA+jI}\cdot)$ transplanted to every rational in $\mathscr U_N$.

nodes.name: $\Omega_{N}^{j, n}$ as a discrete Littlewood-Paley projector
nodes.statement: If we had $\mathscr U_{N}=\{0\}$ then $\Omega_{N}^{j, n}(\xi)$ could be treated as a standard Littlewood--Paley projector. Now we formulate an abstract theorem which can be thought as a discrete variant of Littlewood--Paley theory. Its proof will be based on Theorem \ref{th:3}. Here we only obtain some square function estimate which is interesting in its own right. However, we will be able appreciate its usefulness later, in the proof of inequality \eqref{eq:84}.

nodes.name: Theorem 5 (discrete Littlewood-Paley square function estimate)
nodes.statement: For every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that for all $-\infty\le M_1\le M_2\le \infty$, $j\in\ZZ$ and $N\in\NN$ and every $f\in\ell^p\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Omega_{N}^{j, n}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}\le C_p \log N\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The square function of the arithmetic Littlewood-Paley pieces $\Omega_N^{j,n}$ is $\ell^p$-bounded with a $\log N$ loss, uniformly in $j$ and the truncation range.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5
nodes.statement: By Khinchine's inequality \eqref{eq:23} is equivalent to the following \begin{align} \bigg(\int_0^1\bigg\|\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\varepsilon_n(t)\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Omega_{N}^{j, n}\hat{f}\big)\bigg\|_{\ell^p}^p{\rm d}t\bigg)^{1/p}\lesssim \log N\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} Observe that the multiplier from \eqref{eq:24} can be rewritten as follows \begin{align*} \sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\varepsilon_n(t) \Omega_N^{j, n}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{N}}\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\mathfrak m_n(\xi-a/q)\eta_N(\xi-a/q) \end{align*} with the functions \[ \mathfrak m_n(\xi)=\varepsilon_n(t)\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big). \] We observe that \[ |\mathfrak m_n(\xi)|\lesssim\min\big\{|2^{nA+jI}\xi|_{\infty}, |2^{nA+jI}\xi|_{\infty}^{-1}\big\}. \] The first bound follows from the mean-value theorem, since \[ \big|\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big)\big|= \big|\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big)- \Phi(0)\big|\lesssim\big|2^{nA+jI}\xi\big|\sup_{\xi\in\RR^d}\big|\nabla \Phi(\xi)\big| \lesssim |2^{nA+jI}\xi|_{\infty}. \] The second bound follows since $\Phi$ is a Schwartz function. Moreover, for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is $C_p>0$ such that \[ \big\|\sup_{n\in\ZZ}\big|\calF^{-1}\big(\mathfrak m_n\calF f\big)\big|\big\|_{L^p}\le C_p \|f\|_{L^p} \] for every $f\in L^p\big(\RR^d\big)$. Therefore, by \cite{bigs} the multiplier \[ \sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\mathfrak m_n(\xi) \] corresponds to a continuous singular integral, thus defines a bounded operator on $L^p\big(\RR^d\big)$ for all $p\in(1, \infty)$ with the bound independent of $j\in\ZZ$ and $-\infty\le M_1\le M_2\le \infty$. Hence, Theorem \ref{th:3} applies and the multiplier \[ \sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\varepsilon_n(t) \Omega_N^{j, n}(\xi) \] defines a bounded operator on $\ell^p\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ with the $\log N$ loss, and \eqref{eq:24} is established.
nodes.statement_short: Randomize by Khinchine's inequality, check that $\sum_n \mathfrak m_n$ is a continuous singular-integral multiplier, and apply Theorem 1 to transfer the bound to $\ell^p(\ZZ^d)$ with a $\log N$ loss.

nodes.name: Khinchine randomization
nodes.statement: By Khinchine's inequality \eqref{eq:23} is equivalent to the following \begin{align} \bigg(\int_0^1\bigg\|\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\varepsilon_n(t)\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Omega_{N}^{j, n}\hat{f}\big)\bigg\|_{\ell^p}^p{\rm d}t\bigg)^{1/p}\lesssim \log N\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Replace the square function by a randomized sum with Rademacher signs.

nodes.name: Rewrite the randomized multiplier via $\mathfrak m_n$
nodes.statement: Observe that the multiplier from \eqref{eq:24} can be rewritten as follows \begin{align*} \sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\varepsilon_n(t) \Omega_N^{j, n}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{N}}\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\mathfrak m_n(\xi-a/q)\eta_N(\xi-a/q) \end{align*} with the functions \[ \mathfrak m_n(\xi)=\varepsilon_n(t)\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Recast the randomized multiplier in the form covered by Theorem 1, with $\Theta=\sum_n\mathfrak m_n$.

nodes.name: Pointwise bounds on $\mathfrak m_n$
nodes.statement: We observe that \[ |\mathfrak m_n(\xi)|\lesssim\min\big\{|2^{nA+jI}\xi|_{\infty}, |2^{nA+jI}\xi|_{\infty}^{-1}\big\}. \] The first bound follows from the mean-value theorem, since \[ \big|\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big)\big|= \big|\Phi\big(2^{nA+jI}\xi\big)- \Phi(0)\big|\lesssim\big|2^{nA+jI}\xi\big|\sup_{\xi\in\RR^d}\big|\nabla \Phi(\xi)\big| \lesssim |2^{nA+jI}\xi|_{\infty}. \] The second bound follows since $\Phi$ is a Schwartz function.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathfrak m_n$ vanishes linearly at the origin and decays at infinity.

nodes.name: Identify a continuous singular integral and apply Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Moreover, for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is $C_p>0$ such that \[ \big\|\sup_{n\in\ZZ}\big|\calF^{-1}\big(\mathfrak m_n\calF f\big)\big|\big\|_{L^p}\le C_p \|f\|_{L^p} \] for every $f\in L^p\big(\RR^d\big)$. Therefore, by \cite{bigs} the multiplier \[ \sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\mathfrak m_n(\xi) \] corresponds to a continuous singular integral, thus defines a bounded operator on $L^p\big(\RR^d\big)$ for all $p\in(1, \infty)$ with the bound independent of $j\in\ZZ$ and $-\infty\le M_1\le M_2\le \infty$. Hence, Theorem \ref{th:3} applies and the multiplier \[ \sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\varepsilon_n(t) \Omega_N^{j, n}(\xi) \] defines a bounded operator on $\ell^p\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ with the $\log N$ loss, and \eqref{eq:24} is established.
nodes.statement_short: The continuous multiplier norm is uniformly bounded, so Theorem 1 gives the discrete bound with $\log N$ loss.

nodes.name: Dual form of the discrete Littlewood-Paley inequality
nodes.statement: If the function $\Phi$ is a real-valued function then we have \begin{align} \Big\|\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Omega_{N}^{j, n}\hat{f_n}\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\le C_p \log N\bigg\|\Big(\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}|f_n|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} This is the dual version of inequality \eqref{eq:23} for any sequence of functions $\big(f_n: M_1\le n\le M_2\big)$ such that \[ \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}|f_n|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}<\infty. \]
nodes.statement_short: Dually, superposing the pieces $\Omega_N^{j,n}$ against a vector-valued input is bounded by the square function of the input, with the same $\log N$ loss.
assumptions: the function $\Phi$ is a real-valued function
any sequence of functions $\big(f_n: M_1\le n\le M_2\big)$ such that $\bigg\|\Big(\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}|f_n|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}<\infty$
conclusions: $\Big\|\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Omega_{N}^{j, n}\hat{f_n}\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\le C_p \log N\bigg\|\Big(\sum_{M_1\le n\le M_2}|f_n|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}$

nodes.name: Major-arc projections $\Xi_n$
nodes.statement: Let $\chi>0$ and $l\in\NN$ be the numbers whose precise valued will be adjusted later. As in \cite{mst1} we will consider for every $n\in\NN_0$ the multipliers \begin{align} \Xi_{n}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}}\eta\big(2^{n(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big) \end{align} with $\mathscr U_{N}$ which has been defined in Section \ref{sec:6}.

nodes.name: Logarithmic bound for $\Xi_n$ and the relation $10\rho l=1$
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{th:3} yields, for every $p\in(1, \infty)$, that \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log(n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} The implicit constant in \eqref{eq:54} depends on $\rho>0$ from Theorem \ref{th:3}. From now on we will assume that $l\in\NN$ and $\rho>0$ are related by the equation \begin{align} 10\rho l=1. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1 gives $\|\calF^{-1}(\Xi_n\hat f)\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log(n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}$, with the calibration $10\rho l=1$.

nodes.name: Radon averages $M_N$
nodes.statement: For this purpose we define for every $x\in\ZZ^d$ the Radon averages \[ M_Nf(x)=N^{-k}\sum_{y\in\NN_N^k}f\big(x-\calQ(y)\big). \]
nodes.section: The estimate of the second norm

nodes.name: Maximal function bound for the Radon averages
nodes.statement: From \cite{mst1} follows that for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that for every $f\in\ell^p\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \big\|\sup_{N\in\NN}|M_Nf|\big\|_{\ell^p}\le C_p\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The discrete Radon maximal function is bounded on $\ell^p(\ZZ^d)$ for all $p\in(1,\infty)$.
nodes.section: The estimate of the second norm

nodes.name: Pointwise domination of $T_n$ by the Radon averages
nodes.statement: since we have a pointwise bound \begin{align} \big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\hat{f}\big)(x)\big|=|T_nf(x)|\lesssim M_{2^n}f(x). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $|T_nf|\lesssim M_{2^n}f$ pointwise.
nodes.section: The estimate of the second norm

nodes.name: Major-arc asymptotics for $m_n$ with error $E_{2^n}$
nodes.statement: Note that for any $\xi\in\TT^d$ so that \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}/q|\le 2^{-n(|\gamma|-\chi)} \] for every $\gamma\in \Gamma$ with $1\le q\le e^{n^{1/10}}$ we have \begin{align} m_n(\xi)=G(a/q)\Phi_n(\xi-a/q)+q^{-\delta}E_{2^n}(\xi) \end{align} where \begin{align} |E_{2^n}(\xi)|\lesssim 2^{-n/2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: On the relevant major arcs, $m_n=G(a/q)\Phi_n(\xi-a/q)$ up to an error of size $q^{-\delta}2^{-n/2}$.

nodes.name: Multipliers $\Xi_{n}^j$
nodes.statement: Now for every $j, n\in\NN_0$ we introduce the multipliers \begin{align} \Xi_{n}^j(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}}\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2 \end{align}

nodes.name: Splitting of the major-arc norm into $I_p^1$ and $I_p^2$
nodes.statement: and we note that \begin{align} \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p} &\le \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\sum_{-\chi n\le j<n}m_n\big(\Xi_{n}^j-\Xi_{n}^{j+1}\big)\hat{f}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\\ \nonumber&+\Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}=I_p^1+I_p^2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Telescope $\Xi_n$ through the scales $\Xi_n^j$ and separate the tail term $\Xi_n^n$.

nodes.name: Multipliers $\Delta_{n, s}^j$ and their factorization $\Delta_{n,s}^{j,1}\cdot\Delta_{n,s}^{j,2}$
nodes.statement: Define for any $0\le s< n$ new multipliers \begin{align*} \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2 \end{align*} and we observe that by the definition \eqref{eq:69} we have \begin{align*} \Xi_{n}^j(\xi)-\Xi_{n}^{j+1}(\xi)=\sum_{0\le s<n}\Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi). \end{align*} Moreover, \begin{multline*} \eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi)\big)^2\\ = \big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi)\big)^2\big) \cdot\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+(j-1)I}(\xi)\big)- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+2)I}(\xi)\big)\big). \end{multline*} Thus we see \[ \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}(\xi)\cdot\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}(\xi), \] where \begin{align*} \Delta_{n,s}^{j, 1}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+(j-1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+2)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big) \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The scale-$j$ difference of $\Xi_n$ splits by denominator level $s$ into $\Delta_{n,s}^j$, which factors as a product of two multipliers each satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem 5.

nodes.name: Proof of inequality (84)
nodes.statement:
Let $\chi>0$ and $l\in\NN$ be the numbers whose precise valued will be adjusted later. As in \cite{mst1} we will consider for every $n\in\NN_0$ the multipliers  egin{align} \Xi_{n}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}}\eta ig(2^{n(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q) ig) \end{align} with $\mathscr U_{N}$ which has been defined in Section ef{sec:6}. Theorem ef{th:3} yields, for every $p\in(1, \infty)$, that  egin{align}  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(\Xi_{n}\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log(n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} The implicit constant in \eqref{eq:54} depends on $ho>0$ from Theorem ef{th:3}. From now on we will assume that $l\in\NN$ and $ho>0$ are related by the equation  egin{align} 10ho l=1. \end{align} Assume that $f:\ZZ^d\mapsto\CC$ has finite support and $f\ge0$. Observe that  egin{align} \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}T_{n}f\Big\|_{\ell^p} \le \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\Xi_{n}\hat{f} ig)\Big\|_{\ell^p} + \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f} ig)\Big\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} Without of loss of generality we may assume that $p\ge 2$, the case $1<p\le 2$ follows by the duality then. \subsection{The estimate of the second norm in \eqref{eq:30}} It suffices to show that  egin{align}  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim (n+1)^{-2}\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} For this purpose we define for every $x\in\ZZ^d$ the Radon averages \[ M_Nf(x)=N^{-k}\sum_{y\in\NN_N^k}f ig(x-\calQ(y) ig). \] From \cite{mst1} follows that for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that for every $f\in\ell^p ig(\ZZ^d ig)$ we have  egin{align}  ig\|\sup_{N\in\NN}|M_Nf| ig\|_{\ell^p}\le C_p\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} Then for every $1<p<\infty$ by \eqref{eq:54} and \eqref{eq:55} we obtain  egin{align}  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^p}\le  ig\|\sup_{N\in\NN}M_Nf ig\|_{\ell^p}+ ig\|\sup_{N\in\NN}M_N ig( ig| \mathcal F^{-1} ig(\Xi_{n}\hat{f} ig) ig| ig) ig\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p} \end{align} since we have a pointwise bound  egin{align}  ig|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\hat{f} ig)(x) ig|=|T_nf(x)|\lesssim M_{2^n}f(x). \end{align} We show that it is possible to improve estimate \eqref{eq:21} for $p=2$. Indeed, by Theorem ef{thm:3} we will show that for big enough $\alpha>0$, which will be specified later, and for all $n\in\NN_0$ we have  egin{align}  ig| m_{n}(\xi)(1-\Xi_{n}(\xi)) ig|\lesssim (n+1)^{-\alpha}. \end{align} By Dirichlet's principle we have for every $\gamma\in\Gamma$ \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}/q_{\gamma}|\le q_{\gamma}^{-1}n^{ eta}2^{-n|\gamma|} \] where $1\le q_{\gamma}\le n^{- eta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. In order to apply Theorem ef{thm:3} we must show that there exists some $\gamma\in\Gamma$ such that $n^{ eta}\le q_{\gamma }\le n^{- eta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. Suppose for a contradiction that for every $\gamma \in \Gamma$ we have $1\le q_{\gamma }<n^{ eta} $ then for some $q\le \mathrm{lcm}(q_{\gamma}: \gamma\in\Gamma)\le n^{ eta d}$ we have \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}'/q|\le n^{ eta}2^{-n|\gamma|} \] where $\mathrm{gcd} ig(q, \mathrm{gcd}({a_{\gamma}'}: \gamma\in\Gamma) ig)=1$. Hence, taking $a'=(a_{\gamma}': \gamma\in\Gamma)$ we have $a'/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}$ provided that $ eta d<l$. On the other hand, if $1-\Xi_{n}(\xi)
ot=0$ then for every $a'/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}$ there exists $\gamma\in\Gamma$ such that \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}'/q|>(16d)^{-1} 2^{-n(|\gamma|-\chi)}. \] Therefore \[ 2^{\chi n}<16dn^{ eta} \] but this is impossible when $n\in\NN$ is large. Hence, there is $\gamma\in\Gamma$ such that $n^{ eta}\le q_{\gamma }\le n^{- eta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. Thus by Theorem ef{thm:3} \[ |m_n(\xi)|\lesssim (n+1)^{-\alpha} \] provided that $1-\Xi_{n}(\xi)
ot=0$. This yields \eqref{eq:60} and we obtain  egin{align}  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^2}\lesssim(1+n)^{-\alpha} \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^2}. \end{align} Interpolating \eqref{eq:56} with \eqref{eq:21} we obtain  egin{align}  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim(1+n)^{-c_p\alpha} \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} for some $c_p>0$. Choosing $\alpha>0$ and $l\in\NN$ appropriately large one obtains \eqref{eq:38}. \subsection{The estimate of the first norm in \eqref{eq:30}} Note that for any $\xi\in\TT^d$ so that \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}/q|\le 2^{-n(|\gamma|-\chi)} \] for every $\gamma\in \Gamma$ with $1\le q\le e^{n^{1/10}}$ we have  egin{align} m_n(\xi)=G(a/q)\Phi_n(\xi-a/q)+q^{-\delta}E_{2^n}(\xi) \end{align} where  egin{align} |E_{2^n}(\xi)|\lesssim 2^{-n/2}. \end{align} Proposition ef{prop:0}, with $L_1=2^n$, $L_2=2^{\chi n}$ and $L_3=e^{n^{1/10}}$, establishes \eqref{eq:61} and \eqref{eq:64}, since for sufficiently large $n\in\NN$ we have \[ q^{\delta}|E_{2^n}(\xi)|\lesssim q^{\delta}L_2L_32^{-n}\lesssim  ig(e^{-n((1-\chi)\log 2-2n^{-9/10})} ig)\lesssim 2^{-n/2} \] provided $\chi>0$ is sufficiently small. ig\|_{\ell^p} \lesssim \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} For $p=2$ by Plancherel's theorem and by \eqref{eq:66} we obtain  egin{multline}  ig\|\mathcal F^{-1} ig(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f} ig) ig\|_{\ell^2} =  igg(\int_{\TT^d}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}}|m_{n}(\xi)|^2\eta ig(2^{nA+nI}(\xi-a/q) ig)^4 |\hat{f}(\xi)|^2d\xi igg)^{1/2}\lesssim 2^{-n/(2d)}\|f\|_{\ell^2}. \end{multline} 2^{-\varepsilon n}\|f\|_{\ell^p} \end{align*} which in turn implies \eqref{eq:102} and $I_p^2\lesssim \|f\|_{\ell^p}$. \subsubsection{Bounding $I_p^1$} Define for any $0\le s< n$ new multipliers nodes.statement_short: Split $\sum_n T_n$ into major-arc ($\Xi_n$) and minor-arc ($1-\Xi_n$) parts: the minor arcs are handled by Weyl's inequality (Theorem 4) plus interpolation, and the major arcs by the discrete Littlewood-Paley square function (Theorem 5) together with the $q^{-\delta}$ and $2^{-|j|/d}$ decay of $m_n$.

nodes.name: Introduce $\Xi_n$ and split into major and minor arcs
nodes.statement: Let $\chi>0$ and $l\in\NN$ be the numbers whose precise valued will be adjusted later. As in \cite{mst1} we will consider for every $n\in\NN_0$ the multipliers \begin{align} \Xi_{n}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}}\eta\big(2^{n(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big) \end{align} with $\mathscr U_{N}$ which has been defined in Section \ref{sec:6}. Theorem \ref{th:3} yields, for every $p\in(1, \infty)$, that \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log(n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} The implicit constant in \eqref{eq:54} depends on $\rho>0$ from Theorem \ref{th:3}. From now on we will assume that $l\in\NN$ and $\rho>0$ are related by the equation \begin{align} 10\rho l=1. \end{align} Assume that $f:\ZZ^d\mapsto\CC$ has finite support and $f\ge0$. Observe that \begin{align} \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}T_{n}f\Big\|_{\ell^p} \le \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p} + \Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} Without of loss of generality we may assume that $p\ge 2$, the case $1<p\le 2$ follows by the duality then.
nodes.statement_short: Set up the projections $\Xi_n$, fix $10\rho l=1$, and split the operator into major-arc and minor-arc contributions.

nodes.name: Crude logarithmic bound for the minor-arc term
nodes.statement: \subsection{The estimate of the second norm in \eqref{eq:30}} It suffices to show that \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim (n+1)^{-2}\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} For this purpose we define for every $x\in\ZZ^d$ the Radon averages \[ M_Nf(x)=N^{-k}\sum_{y\in\NN_N^k}f\big(x-\calQ(y)\big). \] From \cite{mst1} follows that for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that for every $f\in\ell^p\big(\ZZ^d\big)$ we have \begin{align} \big\|\sup_{N\in\NN}|M_Nf|\big\|_{\ell^p}\le C_p\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} Then for every $1<p<\infty$ by \eqref{eq:54} and \eqref{eq:55} we obtain \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\le \big\|\sup_{N\in\NN}M_Nf\big\|_{\ell^p}+\big\|\sup_{N\in\NN}M_N\big(\big| \mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}\hat{f}\big)\big|\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p} \end{align} since we have a pointwise bound \begin{align} \big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\hat{f}\big)(x)\big|=|T_nf(x)|\lesssim M_{2^n}f(x). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Dominate the minor-arc piece by the Radon maximal function to get a $\log(n+2)$ bound for all $p$.

nodes.name: Weyl decay for the minor-arc term at $p=2$ and interpolation
nodes.statement: We show that it is possible to improve estimate \eqref{eq:21} for $p=2$. Indeed, by Theorem \ref{thm:3} we will show that for big enough $\alpha>0$, which will be specified later, and for all $n\in\NN_0$ we have \begin{align} \big| m_{n}(\xi)(1-\Xi_{n}(\xi))\big|\lesssim (n+1)^{-\alpha}. \end{align} By Dirichlet's principle we have for every $\gamma\in\Gamma$ \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}/q_{\gamma}|\le q_{\gamma}^{-1}n^{\beta}2^{-n|\gamma|} \] where $1\le q_{\gamma}\le n^{-\beta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. In order to apply Theorem \ref{thm:3} we must show that there exists some $\gamma\in\Gamma$ such that $n^{\beta}\le q_{\gamma }\le n^{-\beta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. Suppose for a contradiction that for every $\gamma \in \Gamma$ we have $1\le q_{\gamma }<n^{\beta} $ then for some $q\le \mathrm{lcm}(q_{\gamma}: \gamma\in\Gamma)\le n^{\beta d}$ we have \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}'/q|\le n^{\beta}2^{-n|\gamma|} \] where $\mathrm{gcd}\big(q, \mathrm{gcd}({a_{\gamma}'}: \gamma\in\Gamma)\big)=1$. Hence, taking $a'=(a_{\gamma}': \gamma\in\Gamma)$ we have $a'/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}$ provided that $\beta d<l$. On the other hand, if $1-\Xi_{n}(\xi)\not=0$ then for every $a'/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}$ there exists $\gamma\in\Gamma$ such that \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}'/q|>(16d)^{-1} 2^{-n(|\gamma|-\chi)}. \] Therefore \[ 2^{\chi n}<16dn^{\beta} \] but this is impossible when $n\in\NN$ is large. Hence, there is $\gamma\in\Gamma$ such that $n^{\beta}\le q_{\gamma }\le n^{-\beta}2^{n|\gamma|}$. Thus by Theorem \ref{thm:3} \[ |m_n(\xi)|\lesssim (n+1)^{-\alpha} \] provided that $1-\Xi_{n}(\xi)\not=0$. This yields \eqref{eq:60} and we obtain \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2}\lesssim(1+n)^{-\alpha} \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^2}. \end{align} Interpolating \eqref{eq:56} with \eqref{eq:21} we obtain \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n(1-\Xi_{n})\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim(1+n)^{-c_p\alpha} \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} for some $c_p>0$. Choosing $\alpha>0$ and $l\in\NN$ appropriately large one obtains \eqref{eq:38}.
nodes.statement_short: Use Dirichlet's principle and a contradiction argument to place $\xi$ in the range of Theorem 4, giving $(n+1)^{-\alpha}$ decay at $p=2$, then interpolate.

nodes.name: Major-arc asymptotics and the split $I_p^1+I_p^2$
nodes.statement: \subsection{The estimate of the first norm in \eqref{eq:30}} Note that for any $\xi\in\TT^d$ so that \[ |\xi_{\gamma}-a_{\gamma}/q|\le 2^{-n(|\gamma|-\chi)} \] for every $\gamma\in \Gamma$ with $1\le q\le e^{n^{1/10}}$ we have \begin{align} m_n(\xi)=G(a/q)\Phi_n(\xi-a/q)+q^{-\delta}E_{2^n}(\xi) \end{align} where \begin{align} |E_{2^n}(\xi)|\lesssim 2^{-n/2}. \end{align} Proposition \ref{prop:0}, with $L_1=2^n$, $L_2=2^{\chi n}$ and $L_3=e^{n^{1/10}}$, establishes \eqref{eq:61} and \eqref{eq:64}, since for sufficiently large $n\in\NN$ we have \[ q^{\delta}|E_{2^n}(\xi)|\lesssim q^{\delta}L_2L_32^{-n}\lesssim \big(e^{-n((1-\chi)\log 2-2n^{-9/10})}\big)\lesssim 2^{-n/2} \] provided $\chi>0$ is sufficiently small. For this purpose observe that by \eqref{eq:61} and \eqref{eq:64} for every $a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}$ we have \begin{align} |m_n(\xi)|&\lesssim q^{-\delta}|\Phi_{n}(\xi-a/q)|+q^{-\delta}|E_{2^n}(\xi)|\\ &\lesssim \nonumber q^{-\delta}\big(\min\big\{1, |2^{nA}(\xi-a/q)|_{\infty}, |2^{nA}(\xi-a/q)|_{\infty}^{-1/d}\big\}+2^{-n/2}\big) \end{align} where the last inequality follows from \eqref{eq:18} and \eqref{eq:19}. Therefore by \eqref{eq:66} we get \begin{align} \big|m_{n}(\xi) \big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2-\eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2\big)\big| \lesssim q^{-\delta}\big(2^{-|j|/d}+2^{-n/2}\big). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 3.1 to get the major-arc asymptotics, telescope $\Xi_n$ into the pieces $\Xi_n^j$, and record the pointwise bounds on $m_n$.

nodes.name: Bounding $I_p^2$
nodes.statement: \subsubsection{Bounding $I_p^2$} It will suffice to show, for some $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_{p}>0$, that \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim 2^{-\varepsilon n}\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} Observe that for any $1<p<\infty$ by \eqref{eq:63}, \eqref{eq:55} and \eqref{eq:54} we have \begin{align} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\le\big\|\sup_{N\in\NN} M_N\big(\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\big|\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p} \lesssim \log (n+2)\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} For $p=2$ by Plancherel's theorem and by \eqref{eq:66} we obtain \begin{multline} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^2} = \bigg(\int_{\TT^d}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{n^l}}|m_{n}(\xi)|^2\eta\big(2^{nA+nI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^4 |\hat{f}(\xi)|^2d\xi\bigg)^{1/2}\lesssim 2^{-n/(2d)}\|f\|_{\ell^2}. \end{multline} Therefore, interpolating \eqref{eq:103} with \eqref{eq:105} we obtain for every $p\in(1, \infty)$ that \begin{align*} \big\|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Xi_{n}^{n}\hat{f}\big)\big\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim 2^{-\varepsilon n}\|f\|_{\ell^p} \end{align*} which in turn implies \eqref{eq:102} and $I_p^2\lesssim \|f\|_{\ell^p}$.
nodes.statement_short: Interpolate the $\log(n+2)$ maximal bound with the $2^{-n/(2d)}$ Plancherel bound to get geometric decay for the tail term $\Xi_n^n$.

nodes.name: Factorize $\Delta_{n,s}^j$ and apply the dual Littlewood-Paley inequality
nodes.statement: \subsubsection{Bounding $I_p^1$} Define for any $0\le s< n$ new multipliers \begin{align*} \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2 \end{align*} and we observe that by the definition \eqref{eq:69} we have \begin{align*} \Xi_{n}^j(\xi)-\Xi_{n}^{j+1}(\xi)=\sum_{0\le s<n}\Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi). \end{align*} Moreover, \begin{multline*} \eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi)\big)^2\\ = \big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi)\big)^2\big) \cdot\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+(j-1)I}(\xi)\big)- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+2)I}(\xi)\big)\big). \end{multline*} Thus we see \[ \Delta_{n, s}^j(\xi)=\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}(\xi)\cdot\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}(\xi), \] where \begin{align*} \Delta_{n,s}^{j, 1}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+(j-1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+2)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big) \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}(\xi)=\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big). \end{align*} Moreover, $\Delta_{n,s}^{j, 1}$ and $\Delta_{n,s}^{j, 2}$ are the multipliers which satisfy the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm:30}. Therefore, \begin{multline} I_p^1=\Big\|\sum_{n\ge0}\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\sum_{-\chi n\le j< n}\sum_{0\le s<n}\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\\ \le \sum_{s\ge0}\sum_{j\in \ZZ}\Big\|\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\mathcal F^{-1}\Big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 1}m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\Big)\Big\|_{\ell^p}\\ \lesssim \sum_{s\ge0}\sum_{j\in\ZZ}\log s\bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}. \end{multline} In the last step we have used \eqref{eq:52}.
nodes.statement_short: Split $\Xi_n^j-\Xi_n^{j+1}$ by denominator level $s$, factor each piece into two Theorem-5 multipliers, and pass to a square function via the dual inequality (52).

nodes.name: Reduce to the decaying square function estimate (73)
nodes.statement: The task now is to show that for some $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_p>0$ \begin{align} \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p} \lesssim s^{-2}2^{-\varepsilon j}\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align} This in turn will imply $I_p^1\lesssim \|f\|_{\ell^p}$ and the proof will be completed. We have assumed that $p\ge 2$, then for every $g\in\ell^r(\ZZ^d)$ such that $g\ge 0$ with $r=(p/2)'>1$ we have by \eqref{eq:63}, the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and \eqref{eq:55} that \begin{multline} \sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\sum_{n\in\ZZ}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)(x)\big|^2g(x) \lesssim \sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\sum_{n\in\ZZ}M_{2^n}\big(\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|\big)(x)^2g(x)\\ \le \sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\sum_{n\in\ZZ}M_{2^n}\big(\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\big)(x)g(x)= \sum_{x\in\ZZ^d}\sum_{n\in\ZZ}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)(x)\big|^2 M_{2^n}^*g(x)\\ \lesssim \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\ZZ}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}^2 \big\|\sup_{N\in\NN} M_N^*g\big\|_{\ell^r} \lesssim \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\ZZ}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^{p}}^2 \|g\|_{\ell^r}. \end{multline} Therefore, by Theorem \ref{thm:30} we have \begin{align} \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\ZZ}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p} \lesssim \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\in\ZZ}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^p}\lesssim \log s\|f\|_{\ell^p}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Remove $m_n$ from the square function by a duality/maximal-function argument and apply Theorem 5 to get a $\log s$ bound in $\ell^p$.

nodes.name: Refine at $p=2$ by Plancherel, interpolate and conclude
nodes.statement: We refine the estimate in \eqref{eq:43} for $p=2$. Indeed, define \[ \varrho_{n, j}(\xi)=\big(\eta\big(2^{nA+jI}(\xi)\big)^2- \eta\big(2^{nA+(j+1)I}(\xi)\big)^2\big) \eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi)\big) \] and \[ \Psi_n(\xi)=\min\big\{|2^{nA}\xi|_{\infty}, |2^{nA}\xi|_{\infty}^{-1/d}, 1\big\}. \] By Plancherel's theorem we have \begin{multline} \bigg\|\Big(\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\big|\mathcal F^{-1}\big(m_n\Delta_{n, s}^{j, 2}\hat{f}\big)\big|^2\Big)^{1/2}\bigg\|_{\ell^2}\\ =\bigg(\int_{\TT^d}\sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}|m_n(\xi)|^2\varrho_{n,j}(\xi-a/q)^2|\hat f(\xi)|^2{\rm d}\xi\bigg)^{1/2}\\ \lesssim (s+1)^{-\delta l}2^{-|j|/(2d)}\|f\|_{\ell^2}. \end{multline} The last estimate is implied by \eqref{eq:66}. Namely, by \eqref{eq:66} we may write \begin{multline} \sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}|m_n(\xi)|^2\varrho_{n,j}(\xi-a/q)^2\\ \lesssim \sum_{n\ge\max\{j,-j/\chi, s\}}\sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}q^{-2\delta}\big(\Psi_n(\xi-a/q)+2^{-n/2}\big)\big(2^{-|j|/d}+2^{-n/2}\big)\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big)^2\\ \lesssim (s+1)^{-2\delta l}2^{-|j|/(2d)}. \end{multline} The last line follows, since we have used the lower bound for $q\ge s^{l}$ if $a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}$. Moreover, \[ \sum_{n\ge0}\big(\Psi_n(\xi-a/q)+2^{-n/2}\big)\lesssim 1 \] and \[ \sum_{a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}}\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big)\lesssim 1 \] by the disjointness of the supports of $\eta\big(2^{s(A-\chi I)}(\xi-a/q)\big)$'s whenever $a/q\in\mathscr U_{(s+1)^l}\setminus\mathscr U_{s^l}$. Since $l\in\NN$ can be as large as we wish thus interpolating \eqref{eq:46} with \eqref{eq:43} we obtain \eqref{eq:73} and the proof of \eqref{eq:84} and consequently Theorem \ref{thm:0} is completed.
nodes.statement_short: Plancherel plus the $q\ge s^l$ lower bound gives $(s+1)^{-\delta l}2^{-|j|/(2d)}$ decay at $p=2$; interpolating with the $\log s$ bound finishes the proof.
